verses.1:1: The book of the lineage of Jesus Christ, the Son of David, the Son of Abraham.
verses.1:2: Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers,
verses.1:3: and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram,
verses.1:4: and Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,
verses.1:5: and Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse,
verses.1:6: and Jesse fathered David the king. And David fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah,
verses.1:7: and Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph,
verses.1:8: and Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah,
verses.1:9: and Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,
verses.1:10: and Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Amos, and Amos fathered Josiah,
verses.1:11: and Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.
verses.1:12: And after the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel,
verses.1:13: and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor,
verses.1:14: and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud,
verses.1:15: and Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob,
verses.1:16: and Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.
verses.1:17: Therefore all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, and from David to the exile to Babylon are fourteen generations, and from the exile to Babylon to the Christ are fourteen generations.
verses.1:18: Now the birth of Jesus Christ came about in this manner: When His mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit.
verses.1:19: And Joseph her husband, being a righteous man and not wishing to expose her to public disgrace, resolved to divorce her secretly.
verses.1:20: But as he pondered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for that which has been conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
verses.1:21: And she shall bear a Son, and you shall call His name Jesus, for He Himself shall save His people from their sins."
verses.1:22: Now all this took place that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
verses.1:23: "Behold, the virgin shall be with child and shall bear a Son, and they shall call His name Immanuel," which is translated, "God is with us."
verses.1:24: And Joseph, awakening from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and took his wife,
verses.1:25: yet he did not know her until she had borne a Son; and he called His name Jesus.
verses.2:1: Now when Jesus had been born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, wise men from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
verses.2:2: saying, "Where is He who was born King of the Jews? For we saw His star in the east, and we have come to worship Him."
verses.2:3: And when King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
verses.2:4: And gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Christ was to be born.
verses.2:5: And they said to him, "In Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it has been written through the prophet:
verses.2:6: 'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you shall come forth a Ruler who shall shepherd My people Israel.'"
verses.2:7: Then Herod, having secretly summoned the wise men, ascertained from them the exact time the star had appeared.
verses.2:8: And sending them to Bethlehem, he said, "Go and search diligently for the young Child; and when you have found Him, report back to me, so that I also may come and worship Him."
verses.2:9: And having heard the king, they departed; and behold, the star that they had seen in the east went before them, until it came and stood over the place where the young Child was.
verses.2:10: And when they saw the star, they rejoiced exceedingly with great joy.
verses.2:11: And coming into the house, they saw the young Child with Mary His mother, and falling down, they worshiped Him; and opening their treasures, they offered to Him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
verses.2:12: And having been warned by God in a dream not to return to Herod, they departed for their own country by another way.
verses.2:13: Now after they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Arise, take the young Child and His mother, and flee into Egypt, and remain there until I tell you; for Herod is about to seek the young Child to destroy Him."
verses.2:14: So he arose and took the young Child and His mother by night, and departed into Egypt,
verses.2:15: and remained there until the death of Herod, that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "Out of Egypt I have called My Son."
verses.2:16: Then Herod, seeing that he had been outwitted by the wise men, became exceedingly furious; and he sent and slew all the male children in Bethlehem and in all its surrounding region, from two years old and under, according to the time that he had ascertained from the wise men.
verses.2:17: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying:
verses.2:18: "A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; and she would not be comforted, because they are no more."
verses.2:19: Now after Herod had died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
verses.2:20: saying, "Arise, take the young Child and His mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the life of the young Child are dead."
verses.2:21: So he arose, took the young Child and His mother, and entered the land of Israel.
verses.2:22: Yet when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there; and having been warned by God in a dream, he withdrew into the district of Galilee.
verses.2:23: And arriving there, he dwelt in a city called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled, "He shall be called a Nazarene."
verses.3:1: Now in those days John the Baptist appeared, preaching in the wilderness of Judea,
verses.3:2: saying, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near!"
verses.3:3: For this is he who was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, "The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight His paths.'"
verses.3:4: Now John himself wore a garment of camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
verses.3:5: Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him,
verses.3:6: and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
verses.3:7: But seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, "Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
verses.3:8: Therefore bring forth fruit worthy of repentance,
verses.3:9: and do not presume to say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father'; for I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham.
verses.3:10: Even now the ax is already laid at the root of the trees; therefore every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire.
verses.3:11: I indeed baptize you with water for repentance, yet He who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; He Himself shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.3:12: His winnowing fork is in His hand, and He shall thoroughly cleanse His threshing floor and gather His wheat into the barn, but the chaff He shall burn up with unquenchable fire."
verses.3:13: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
verses.3:14: But he tried to prevent Him, saying, "I have need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?"
verses.3:15: Yet Jesus answered and said to him, "Permit it at this time, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then he permitted Him.
verses.3:16: And having been baptized, Jesus immediately came up from the water; and behold, the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, coming upon Him.
verses.3:17: And behold, a voice came from the heavens, saying, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I take great delight."
verses.4:1: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tempted by the devil.
verses.4:2: And having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward He became hungry.
verses.4:3: And drawing near, the tempter said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, command that these stones become loaves of bread."
verses.4:4: But He answered and said, "It is written, 'Not by bread alone shall man live, but by every word going forth through the mouth of God.'"
verses.4:5: Then the devil took Him into the holy city, and placed Him upon the pinnacle of the temple,
verses.4:6: and said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, cast Yourself down; for it is written, 'He shall command His angels concerning You, and upon their hands they shall lift You up, lest You strike Your foot against a stone.'"
verses.4:7: Jesus said to him, "Again it is written, 'You shall not test the Lord your God.'"
verses.4:8: Again the devil took Him to an exceedingly high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
verses.4:9: and said to Him, "I will give all these things to You, if You fall down and worship me."
verses.4:10: Then Jesus said to him, "Depart, Satan! For it is written, 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone you shall serve.'"
verses.4:11: Then the devil left Him, and behold, angels drew near and ministered to Him.
verses.4:12: Now when He heard that John had been delivered up, He withdrew into Galilee.
verses.4:13: And leaving Nazareth, He came and dwelt in Capernaum by the sea, within the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali,
verses.4:14: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
verses.4:15: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, along the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
verses.4:16: the people sitting in darkness have seen a great light, and to those sitting in the region and shadow of death, light has dawned upon them."
verses.4:17: From that time Jesus began to preach and to say, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near."
verses.4:18: Now as He walked beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon who is called Peter and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
verses.4:19: And He said to them, "Come after Me, and I will make you fishers of men."
verses.4:20: And immediately leaving their nets, they followed Him.
verses.4:21: And proceeding from there, He saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets; and He called them.
verses.4:22: And immediately leaving the boat and their father, they followed Him.
verses.4:23: And He went about throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people.
verses.4:24: And the report of Him went forth into all Syria; and they brought to Him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, those possessed by demons, and epileptics, and paralytics; and He healed them.
verses.4:25: And great multitudes followed Him from Galilee and Decapolis, and Jerusalem and Judea, and beyond the Jordan.
verses.5:1: Now when He saw the multitudes, He ascended the mountain; and after He had sat down, His disciples drew near to Him.
verses.5:2: And opening His mouth, He began to teach them, saying:
verses.5:3: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for to them belongs the kingdom of heaven.
verses.5:4: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall receive comfort.
verses.5:5: Blessed are the meek, for they themselves shall inherit the earth.
verses.5:6: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be fully satisfied.
verses.5:7: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall find mercy.
verses.5:8: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall behold God.
verses.5:9: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they themselves shall be called sons of God.
verses.5:10: Blessed are those who have been persecuted on account of righteousness, for to them belongs the kingdom of heaven.
verses.5:11: Blessed are you when men reproach you and persecute you, and falsely speak every kind of evil against you for My sake.
verses.5:12: Rejoice and exult, for your reward in heaven is abundant; for in the same manner they persecuted the prophets who went before you.
verses.5:13: You are the salt of the earth; yet if the salt loses its savor, with what shall it be salted? It is no longer good for anything except to be cast outside and trampled underfoot by men.
verses.5:14: You are the light of the world. A city situated upon a mountain cannot be concealed;
verses.5:15: neither do men light a lamp and place it beneath a measuring basket, but upon the lampstand, and it shines upon all who are in the house.
verses.5:16: In like manner let your light shine before men, so that they may behold your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
verses.5:17: Do not suppose that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfill.
verses.5:18: For assuredly, I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke of a letter shall by any means pass away from the Law, until all things come to pass.
verses.5:19: Therefore, whoever sets aside one of the least of these commandments and teaches men to do the same shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever practices and teaches them, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.5:20: For I say to you that unless your righteousness surpasses that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall by no means enter into the kingdom of heaven.
verses.5:21: You have heard that it was spoken to those of old, 'You shall not murder, and whoever murders shall be liable to the judgment.'
verses.5:22: But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to the judgment; and whoever says to his brother, 'Raca,' shall be liable to the Sanhedrin; and whoever says, 'You fool,' shall be liable to the fire of hell.
verses.5:23: Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother holds something against you,
verses.5:24: leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled with your brother, and then come and present your gift.
verses.5:25: Come to terms quickly with your adversary while you are with him on the way, lest the adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be cast into prison.
verses.5:26: Assuredly, I say to you, you shall by no means come forth from there until you have paid the very last copper coin.
verses.5:27: You have heard that it was spoken, 'You shall not commit adultery.'
verses.5:28: But I say to you that everyone who looks upon a woman in order to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
verses.5:29: Now if your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and cast it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish, and not that your whole body be cast into hell.
verses.5:30: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish, and not that your whole body depart into hell.
verses.5:31: It was also spoken, 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a decree of divorce.'
verses.5:32: But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
verses.5:33: Again, you have heard that it was spoken to those of old, 'You shall not swear falsely, but you shall fulfill your oaths to the Lord.'
verses.5:34: But I say to you, do not swear an oath at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
verses.5:35: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of His feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King;
verses.5:36: neither shall you swear by your head, for you are unable to make a single hair white or black.
verses.5:37: Rather, let your word be 'Yes, yes,' 'No, no'; for anything beyond these comes from the evil one.
verses.5:38: You have heard that it was spoken, 'An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.'
verses.5:39: But I say to you, do not resist one who is evil; rather, whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other as well;
verses.5:40: and to him who wishes to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;
verses.5:41: and whoever presses you into service for one mile, go with him two.
verses.5:42: Give to the one who asks of you, and do not turn away from the one who desires to borrow from you.
verses.5:43: You have heard that it was spoken, 'You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
verses.5:44: But I say to you, love your enemies and pray on behalf of those who persecute you,
verses.5:45: so that you may become sons of your Father who is in heaven; for He causes His sun to rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.
verses.5:46: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the very same?
verses.5:47: And if you greet only your brethren, what extraordinary thing do you do? Do not even the Gentiles do the very same?
verses.5:48: Therefore, you yourselves shall be perfect, even as your heavenly Father is perfect."
verses.6:1: Take heed not to practice your righteousness before men in order to be beheld by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.
verses.6:2: Therefore, whenever you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by men. Assuredly, I say to you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.6:3: But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
verses.6:4: so that your almsgiving may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
verses.6:5: And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites; for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the corners of the broad streets, so that they may be seen by men. Assuredly, I say to you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.6:6: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner chamber, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
verses.6:7: And while praying, do not babble with idle words as the Gentiles do, for they suppose that they will be heard because of their many words.
verses.6:8: Therefore do not become like them; for your Father knows the things of which you have need before you ask Him.
verses.6:9: Therefore pray in this manner: "Our Father who is in the heavens, hallowed be Your name;
verses.6:10: let Your kingdom come; let Your will be done, as in heaven, so also upon earth.
verses.6:11: Give to us this day our daily bread;
verses.6:12: and forgive us our debts, even as we also have forgiven our debtors;
verses.6:13: and do not bring us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one."
verses.6:14: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will forgive you also;
verses.6:15: but if you do not forgive men, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
verses.6:16: Moreover, when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites; for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to men to be fasting. Assuredly, I say to you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.6:17: Yet you, while fasting, anoint your head and wash your face,
verses.6:18: so that you may not appear to men to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
verses.6:19: Do not store up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break through and steal;
verses.6:20: but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break through nor steal;
verses.6:21: for where your treasure is, there also your heart will be.
verses.6:22: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore, if your eye is sound, your whole body shall be full of light;
verses.6:23: but if your eye is evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
verses.6:24: No one is able to serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold fast to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
verses.6:25: For this reason I say to you, do not be anxious about your life, what you shall eat or what you shall drink, nor about your body, what you shall put on. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
verses.6:26: Behold the birds of the air, for they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of far greater worth than they?
verses.6:27: And which of you by being anxious is able to add one cubit to his stature?
verses.6:28: And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider well the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin;
verses.6:29: yet I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these.
verses.6:30: Now if God so clothes the grass of the field, which exists today and tomorrow is cast into the oven, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
verses.6:31: Therefore do not be anxious, saying, "What shall we eat?" or, "What shall we drink?" or, "What shall we wear?"
verses.6:32: For all these things the Gentiles eagerly seek; for your heavenly Father knows that you have need of all these things.
verses.6:33: Rather, seek first the kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.
verses.6:34: Therefore do not be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow shall be anxious for itself; enough for the day is its own trouble.
verses.7:1: Do not judge, lest you be judged;
verses.7:2: for with the judgment by which you judge, you shall be judged; and with the measure by which you measure, it shall be measured to you.
verses.7:3: And why do you look upon the speck that is in your brother's eye, yet do not consider the beam that is in your own eye?
verses.7:4: Or how will you say to your brother, "Let me cast out the speck from your eye," and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
verses.7:5: Hypocrite! First cast out the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to cast out the speck from your brother's eye.
verses.7:6: Do not give what is holy to the dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them beneath their feet, and turning, tear you to pieces.
verses.7:7: Ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you.
verses.7:8: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it shall be opened.
verses.7:9: Or what man is there among you who, if his son asks him for bread—will he give him a stone?
verses.7:10: Or if he also asks for a fish—will he give him a serpent?
verses.7:11: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father who is in the heavens give good things to those who ask Him!
verses.7:12: In all things, therefore, whatever you desire that men should do to you, even so do to them also; for this is the Law and the Prophets.
verses.7:13: Enter through the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it;
verses.7:14: for narrow is the gate and hard is the way that leads to life, and few are those who find it.
verses.7:15: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, yet inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
verses.7:16: By their fruits you shall recognize them. Do men gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
verses.7:17: Even so, every good tree produces fine fruit, but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit;
verses.7:18: a good tree is not able to bear evil fruit, nor is a corrupt tree able to produce fine fruit.
verses.7:19: Every tree that does not produce fine fruit is cut down and cast into the fire.
verses.7:20: Therefore, by their fruits you shall recognize them.
verses.7:21: Not everyone who says to Me, "Lord, Lord," shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of My Father who is in heaven.
verses.7:22: Many will say to Me in that day, "Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name cast out demons, and in Your name perform many mighty works?"
verses.7:23: And then I will declare to them, "I never knew you; depart from Me, you who work lawlessness."
verses.7:24: Therefore, everyone who hears these words of Mine and practices them shall be likened to a wise man who built his house upon the rock.
verses.7:25: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.
verses.7:26: And everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not practice them shall be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.
verses.7:27: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew and struck against that house; and it fell, and its fall was great.
verses.7:28: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that the multitudes were astonished at His teaching;
verses.7:29: for He was teaching them as one possessing authority, and not as their scribes.
verses.8:1: Now when He descended from the mountain, many multitudes followed Him.
verses.8:2: And behold, a leper approached and worshiped Him, saying, "Lord, if You are willing, You are able to cleanse me."
verses.8:3: And stretching forth His hand, He touched him, saying, "I am willing; be cleansed." And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
verses.8:4: And Jesus said to him, "See that you tell no one; rather go, show yourself to the priest, and present the gift which Moses commanded, as a witness to them."
verses.8:5: Now when He had entered Capernaum, a centurion approached Him, imploring Him
verses.8:6: and saying, "Lord, my servant lies paralyzed in the house, grievously tormented."
verses.8:7: And He said to him, "I Myself will come and heal him."
verses.8:8: And in reply the centurion said, "Lord, I am not worthy that You should enter beneath my roof; rather, speak only with a word, and my servant shall be healed.
verses.8:9: For I also am a man set under authority, having soldiers under myself; and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes, and to another, 'Come,' and he comes, and to my bondservant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
verses.8:10: Now when Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those who followed, "Assuredly, I say to you, with no one in Israel have I found such great faith.
verses.8:11: And I tell you that many shall come from east and west, and shall recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
verses.8:12: but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast out into the outer darkness; in that place there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
verses.8:13: Then Jesus said to the centurion, "Go; let it be done for you even as you have believed." And the servant was healed in that very hour.
verses.8:14: And upon entering the house of Peter, Jesus saw his mother-in-law lying sick and stricken with a fever.
verses.8:15: And He touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she arose and ministered to Him.
verses.8:16: Now when evening had come, they brought to Him many who were demon-possessed; and He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were afflicted,
verses.8:17: in order that what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, saying, "He Himself took up our infirmities and bore our diseases."
verses.8:18: Now when Jesus saw a multitude around Him, He gave command to depart to the other side.
verses.8:19: And a certain scribe approached and said to Him, "Teacher, I will follow You wherever You may go."
verses.8:20: And Jesus said to him, "The foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, yet the Son of Man has no place where He may lay His head."
verses.8:21: And another of the disciples said to Him, "Lord, permit me first to depart and bury my father."
verses.8:22: But Jesus said to him, "Follow Me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
verses.8:23: And when He stepped into a boat, His disciples followed Him.
verses.8:24: And behold, a fierce tempest arose upon the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; yet He Himself was sleeping.
verses.8:25: And coming to Him, they awakened Him, saying, "Lord, save us; we are perishing!"
verses.8:26: And He said to them, "Why are you fearful, you of little faith?" Then rising up, He rebuked the winds and the sea, and there came a great calm.
verses.8:27: And the men were amazed, saying, "What sort of man is this, that both the winds and the sea obey Him?"
verses.8:28: Now when He had come to the other side, into the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men met Him as they came forth from the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that no one was able to pass along that way.
verses.8:29: And behold, they cried out, saying, "What is there between us and You, Son of God? Have You come here to torment us before the time?"
verses.8:30: Now at a distance from them, a herd of many swine was feeding.
verses.8:31: So the demons implored Him, saying, "If You cast us out, send us into the herd of swine."
verses.8:32: And He said to them, "Go." And coming out, they departed into the swine; and behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and died in the waters.
verses.8:33: Then those who tended them fled, and going into the city, they reported everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
verses.8:34: And behold, the entire city came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw Him, they urged Him to depart from their borders.
verses.9:1: And stepping into a boat, He crossed over and came to His own city.
verses.9:2: And behold, they brought to Him a paralyzed man lying upon a bed. And seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralytic, "Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven."
verses.9:3: And behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, "This man blasphemes!"
verses.9:4: And Jesus, seeing their thoughts, said, "Why do you ponder evil in your hearts?
verses.9:5: For which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Arise and walk'?
verses.9:6: But in order that you may know that the Son of Man has authority upon the earth to forgive sins"—then He said to the paralytic, "Rise, pick up your bed, and go to your house."
verses.9:7: And rising up, he departed to his house.
verses.9:8: Now when the multitudes saw this, they were struck with fear and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
verses.9:9: And as Jesus passed on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax office, and He said to him, "Follow Me." And rising up, he followed Him.
verses.9:10: And it came to pass, as He reclined at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined together with Jesus and His disciples.
verses.9:11: And upon seeing this, the Pharisees spoke to His disciples, "Why is your Teacher eating with the tax collectors and sinners?"
verses.9:12: Yet when He heard this, He said, "Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill.
verses.9:13: Go now and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
verses.9:14: Then the disciples of John approached Him, saying, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast, whereas Your disciples do not fast?"
verses.9:15: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber mourn so long as the bridegroom is with them? Yet days shall come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then they shall fast.
verses.9:16: Moreover, no one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth upon an old garment; for its patch tears away from the garment, and a worse rent is made.
verses.9:17: Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, and the wine is spilled, and the wineskins are ruined; rather, they pour new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved."
verses.9:18: While He was speaking these things to them, behold, a certain ruler came and worshiped Him, saying, "My daughter has just now died; yet come, lay Your hand upon her, and she shall live."
verses.9:19: And Jesus arose and followed him, and His disciples also.
verses.9:20: And behold, a woman who had suffered a flow of blood for twelve years approached from behind and touched the fringe of His garment;
verses.9:21: for she was saying within herself, "If I only touch His garment, I shall be made well."
verses.9:22: Then Jesus, turning and seeing her, said, "Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well." And the woman was made well from that very hour.
verses.9:23: And when Jesus came into the house of the ruler and saw the flute players and the crowd making a noisy commotion,
verses.9:24: He said, "Withdraw, for the girl has not died, but is sleeping." And they laughed Him to scorn.
verses.9:25: Yet when the crowd had been put outside, He went in and took hold of her hand, and the girl arose.
verses.9:26: And the report of this went forth into all that land.
verses.9:27: And as Jesus departed from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out and saying, "Have mercy upon us, Son of David!"
verses.9:28: Now when He had come into the house, the blind men approached Him; and Jesus said to them, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" They said to Him, "Yes, Lord."
verses.9:29: Then He touched their eyes, saying, "According to your faith, let it be done for you."
verses.9:30: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly charged them, saying, "See to it that no one knows of this."
verses.9:31: Yet having gone out, they spread His fame throughout all that land.
verses.9:32: Now as they were going out, behold, they brought to Him a mute man who was demon-possessed.
verses.9:33: And when the demon was cast out, the mute man spoke; and the multitudes marveled, saying, "Never was anything like this seen in Israel!"
verses.9:34: Yet the Pharisees were saying, "By the ruler of the demons He casts out the demons."
verses.9:35: And Jesus went about through all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity.
verses.9:36: And when He saw the multitudes, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and cast down, like sheep having no shepherd.
verses.9:37: Then He said to His disciples, "The harvest indeed is plentiful, yet the laborers are few;
verses.9:38: pray therefore to the Lord of the harvest that He may send forth laborers into His harvest."
verses.10:1: And having summoned His twelve disciples to Himself, He granted them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every infirmity.
verses.10:2: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; and James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
verses.10:3: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
verses.10:4: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed Him.
verses.10:5: These twelve Jesus sent forth, charging them and saying, "Do not depart into the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans;
verses.10:6: but go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
verses.10:7: And as you go, proclaim, saying, 'The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.'
verses.10:8: Heal those who are sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Without cost you have received; without cost give.
verses.10:9: Acquire neither gold, nor silver, nor copper for your belts,
verses.10:10: nor a provision bag for the journey, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the laborer is worthy of his sustenance.
verses.10:11: Now whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and abide there until you depart.
verses.10:12: And as you enter the house, greet it.
verses.10:13: And if indeed the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; yet if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
verses.10:14: And whoever will not receive you nor listen to your words, as you go forth out of that house or city, shake off the dust from your feet.
verses.10:15: Assuredly, I say to you, it shall be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.
verses.10:16: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore be prudent as serpents and guileless as doves.
verses.10:17: Yet beware of men, for they shall deliver you up to councils and scourge you in their synagogues.
verses.10:18: And you shall even be brought before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
verses.10:19: Yet when they deliver you up, do not be anxious about how or what you shall speak; for it shall be given to you in that hour what you shall speak.
verses.10:20: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
verses.10:21: Now brother shall deliver up brother to death, and a father his child; and children shall rise up against parents and put them to death.
verses.10:22: And you shall be hated by all on account of My name; yet he who endures to the end, this one shall be saved.
verses.10:23: Now when they persecute you in this city, flee to the next; for assuredly, I say to you, you shall by no means finish going through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes.
verses.10:24: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor is a bondservant above his master.
verses.10:25: It is sufficient for the disciple that he become like his teacher, and the bondservant like his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!
verses.10:26: Therefore do not fear them; for nothing is veiled that shall not be revealed, and nothing hidden that shall not be made known.
verses.10:27: What I speak to you in the darkness, declare in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim upon the housetops.
verses.10:28: And do not fear those who slay the body yet are unable to slay the soul; rather, fear Him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
verses.10:29: Are not two sparrows sold for a small copper coin? Yet not one of them shall fall to the ground apart from your Father.
verses.10:30: And as for you, even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
verses.10:31: Do not fear, therefore; you are of greater worth than many sparrows.
verses.10:32: Everyone therefore who shall confess Me before men, him I also shall confess before My Father who is in heaven;
verses.10:33: yet whoever denies Me before men, him I also shall deny before My Father who is in heaven.
verses.10:34: Do not suppose that I came to cast peace upon the earth; I did not come to cast peace, but a sword.
verses.10:35: For I came to divide a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;
verses.10:36: and a man's enemies shall be those of his own household.
verses.10:37: The one who loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; and the one who loves son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me.
verses.10:38: And he who does not take up his cross and follow after Me is not worthy of Me.
verses.10:39: The one who finds his life shall lose it, and the one who loses his life for My sake shall find it.
verses.10:40: He who welcomes you welcomes Me, and he who welcomes Me welcomes Him who sent Me.
verses.10:41: He who welcomes a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward, and he who welcomes a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man's reward.
verses.10:42: And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, assuredly, I say to you, he shall by no means lose his reward."
verses.11:1: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, that He departed from there to teach and to preach in their cities.
verses.11:2: Now when John heard in prison of the works of the Christ, he sent word through his disciples
verses.11:3: and said to Him, "Are You the Coming One, or shall we look for another?"
verses.11:4: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Go and report to John the things which you hear and see:
verses.11:5: the blind recover their sight and the lame walk; lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear; and the dead are raised and the poor have the gospel proclaimed to them.
verses.11:6: And blessed is he who does not stumble on account of Me."
verses.11:7: Now as these were departing, Jesus began to speak to the multitudes concerning John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to gaze upon? A reed shaken by the wind?
verses.11:8: Yet what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft apparel? Behold, those who wear soft apparel are in the houses of kings.
verses.11:9: Then why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
verses.11:10: This is he concerning whom it is written: 'Behold, I send My messenger before Your face, who shall prepare Your way before You.'
verses.11:11: Assuredly, I say to you, among those born of women there has not arisen one greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
verses.11:12: And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and violent men seize it by force.
verses.11:13: For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
verses.11:14: And if you are willing to receive it, he himself is Elijah who is to come.
verses.11:15: Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
verses.11:16: Yet to what shall I liken this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces who call out to the others
verses.11:17: and say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn.'
verses.11:18: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'
verses.11:19: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!' Yet wisdom is vindicated by her works."
verses.11:20: Then He began to reproach the cities in which most of His mighty works had been performed, because they did not repent:
verses.11:21: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works which were performed in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.11:22: Nevertheless, I say to you, it shall be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judgment than for you.
verses.11:23: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You shall descend to Hades! For if the mighty works which were performed in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this very day.
verses.11:24: Nevertheless, I say to you that it shall be more bearable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for you."
verses.11:25: At that time Jesus answered and said, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have concealed these things from the wise and discerning, and have revealed them to little children.
verses.11:26: Yes, Father, for thus it was well-pleasing in Your sight.
verses.11:27: All things were delivered to Me by My Father, and no one truly knows the Son except the Father; nor does anyone truly know the Father except the Son, and he to whom the Son wills to reveal Him.
verses.11:28: Come to Me, all you who toil and are heavily burdened, and I shall give you rest.
verses.11:29: Take up My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am meek and humble in heart, and you shall find rest for your souls;
verses.11:30: for My yoke is gentle, and My burden is light."
verses.12:1: At that time Jesus passed through the grainfields on the Sabbath; and His disciples became hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
verses.12:2: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to Him, "Behold, Your disciples are doing what it is not lawful to do on the Sabbath."
verses.12:3: And He said to them, "Have you not read what David did when he became hungry, and those who were with him,
verses.12:4: how he entered into the house of God, and they ate the showbread, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but for the priests alone?
verses.12:5: Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?
verses.12:6: Yet I say to you, something greater than the temple is in this place.
verses.12:7: And if you had understood what it means, 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned the guiltless.
verses.12:8: For the Son of Man is the Lord of the Sabbath."
verses.12:9: And departing from that place, He came into their synagogue.
verses.12:10: And behold, a man was there who had a withered hand. And they questioned Him, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" so that they might accuse Him.
verses.12:11: And He said to them, "What man among you who owns one sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it up?
verses.12:12: How much greater in worth, then, is a man than a sheep! Thus it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath."
verses.12:13: Then He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." So he stretched it out, and it was restored sound, like the other.
verses.12:14: But when the Pharisees went out, they took counsel against Him as to how they might destroy Him.
verses.12:15: Yet Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from that place; and many followed Him, and He healed them all,
verses.12:16: and He strictly charged them that they should not make Him known,
verses.12:17: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
verses.12:18: "Behold, My Servant whom I have chosen, My Beloved in whom My soul delights; I will place My Spirit upon Him, and He shall proclaim justice to the Gentiles.
verses.12:19: He will not strive nor cry aloud, nor shall anyone hear His voice in the streets.
verses.12:20: A bruised reed He shall not break, and a smoldering wick He shall not quench, until He brings justice forth to victory;
verses.12:21: and in His name the Gentiles shall hope."
verses.12:22: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Him; and He healed him, so that the mute man spoke and saw.
verses.12:23: And all the multitudes were astonished and were saying, "Can this be the Son of David?"
verses.12:24: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, "This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons."
verses.12:25: And knowing their thoughts, He said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand.
verses.12:26: And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how, then, shall his kingdom stand?
verses.12:27: And if I by Beelzebul cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? For this reason they themselves shall be your judges.
verses.12:28: Yet if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then indeed the kingdom of God has come upon you.
verses.12:29: Or how can anyone enter into the house of the strong man and seize his property, unless he first binds the strong man? And then he shall plunder his house.
verses.12:30: The one who is not with Me is against Me, and the one who does not gather with Me scatters.
verses.12:31: For this reason I say to you, every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven men, yet the blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven.
verses.12:32: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, either in this age or in the coming one.
verses.12:33: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; for by its fruit the tree is known.
verses.12:34: Offspring of vipers! How are you able to speak good things, being evil? For from the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
verses.12:35: The good man from the good treasury brings forth good things, and the evil man from the evil treasury brings forth evil things.
verses.12:36: Yet I say to you that for every idle word which men shall speak, they shall render an account concerning it on the day of judgment;
verses.12:37: for from your words you shall be justified, and from your words you shall be condemned."
verses.12:38: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered Him, saying, "Teacher, we wish to see a sign from You."
verses.12:39: But answering, He said to them, "A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, yet no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
verses.12:40: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the great fish three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
verses.12:41: The men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
verses.12:42: The queen of the South shall rise up in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
verses.12:43: Now when the unclean spirit goes out from a man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find any.
verses.12:44: Then it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came out.' And having come, it finds it unoccupied, swept, and put in order.
verses.12:45: Then it goes and takes along with itself seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and entering in, they dwell there; and the final state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so shall it be with this wicked generation."
verses.12:46: While He was still speaking to the multitudes, behold, His mother and brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to Him.
verses.12:47: And someone said to Him, "Behold, Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to You."
verses.12:48: But answering, He said to the one who spoke to Him, "Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?"
verses.12:49: And stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He said, "Behold, My mother and My brothers!
verses.12:50: For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, that one is My brother and sister and mother."
verses.13:1: On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea.
verses.13:2: And great multitudes were gathered together to Him, so that He entered a boat and sat down; and the entire multitude stood on the shore.
verses.13:3: And He spoke many things to them in parables, saying, "Behold, a sower went forth to sow.
verses.13:4: And as he sowed, some fell along the pathway, and the birds came and devoured them.
verses.13:5: Others fell on rocky places, where they did not have much earth; and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil.
verses.13:6: But when the sun had risen, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.
verses.13:7: And others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.
verses.13:8: But others fell on the good ground and yielded fruit: some a hundred, some sixty, and some thirty.
verses.13:9: He who has ears, let him hear."
verses.13:10: And the disciples came near and said to Him, "Why do You speak to them in parables?"
verses.13:11: And He answered and said to them, "Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.
verses.13:12: For whoever has, to him it shall be given, and he shall have an abundance; yet whoever does not have, even what he has shall be taken from him.
verses.13:13: For this reason I speak to them in parables: because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
verses.13:14: And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says, 'With hearing you shall hear and shall by no means understand, and seeing you shall see and shall by no means perceive;
verses.13:15: for the heart of this people has grown calloused, and with their ears they have scarcely heard, and their eyes they have shut; lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I shall heal them.'
verses.13:16: Yet blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
verses.13:17: For assuredly, I say to you that many prophets and righteous men longed to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.
verses.13:18: You, therefore, hear the parable of the sower:
verses.13:19: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart. This is the one who was sown along the pathway.
verses.13:20: And the one who was sown on the rocky places, this is he who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy;
verses.13:21: yet he has no root in himself, but lasts only for a season; and when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he stumbles.
verses.13:22: And the one who was sown among the thorns, this is he who hears the word, and the anxiety of the age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.13:23: But the one who was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and produces: some a hundred, some sixty, and some thirty."
verses.13:24: Another parable He set before them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven may be likened to a man who sowed good seed in his field.
verses.13:25: But while men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went away.
verses.13:26: And when the blade sprouted and brought forth fruit, then the tares appeared also.
verses.13:27: So the servants of the householder came near and said to him, 'Sir, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where then does it have tares?'
verses.13:28: And he said to them, 'An enemy has done this.' The servants said to him, 'Do you desire then that we go and gather them up?'
verses.13:29: But he said, 'No, lest while gathering the tares you uproot the wheat together with them.
verses.13:30: Let both grow together until the harvest; and in the season of harvest I will say to the reapers, "First gather the tares and bind them into bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn."'"
verses.13:31: Another parable He set before them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field;
verses.13:32: which indeed is the smallest of all seeds, yet when it has grown, it is greater than the garden herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and lodge in its branches."
verses.13:33: Another parable He spoke to them: "The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal until the whole was leavened."
verses.13:34: All these things Jesus spoke to the multitudes in parables, and without a parable He spoke nothing to them,
verses.13:35: that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "I will open My mouth in parables; I will declare things kept hidden from the foundation of the world."
verses.13:36: Then, leaving the multitudes, He came into the house. And His disciples approached Him, saying, "Explain to us the parable of the tares of the field."
verses.13:37: And He answered and said, "The One who sows the good seed is the Son of Man;
verses.13:38: and the field is the world; as for the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom, while the tares are the sons of the evil one;
verses.13:39: and the enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the consummation of the age, and the reapers are angels.
verses.13:40: Therefore, just as the tares are gathered and burned in fire, so it shall be at the consummation of the age.
verses.13:41: The Son of Man shall send forth His angels, and they shall gather out of His kingdom all things that cause stumbling and those who practice lawlessness,
verses.13:42: and they shall cast them into the furnace of fire; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
verses.13:43: Then the righteous shall shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear.
verses.13:44: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and concealed; and in his joy he goes and sells all that he possesses and buys that field.
verses.13:45: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls;
verses.13:46: and upon finding one pearl of great value, he went and sold all that he possessed and bought it.
verses.13:47: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea, gathering of every kind;
verses.13:48: which, when it was full, they drew up onto the shore; and sitting down, they gathered the good into vessels, but the bad they cast out.
verses.13:49: So it shall be at the consummation of the age: the angels shall come forth and separate the wicked from the midst of the righteous,
verses.13:50: and they shall cast them into the furnace of fire; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
verses.13:51: Have you understood all these things?" They said to Him, "Yes."
verses.13:52: And He said to them, "Therefore every scribe who has been discipled for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings forth out of his treasure things new and old."
verses.13:53: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, that He departed from there.
verses.13:54: And having come to His own homeland, He taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, "From where did this Man obtain this wisdom and these mighty works?
verses.13:55: Is this not the carpenter's son? Is His mother not called Mary, and His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
verses.13:56: And His sisters, are they not all with us? From where then did this Man obtain all these things?"
verses.13:57: And they took offense at Him. But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his homeland and in his own house."
verses.13:58: And He did not perform many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
verses.14:1: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,
verses.14:2: and said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he has been raised from the dead, and for this reason these powers are active in him."
verses.14:3: For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him away in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother,
verses.14:4: for John was saying to him, "It is not lawful for you to have her."
verses.14:5: And though he wished to slay him, he feared the multitude, because they held him to be a prophet.
verses.14:6: Now when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst and pleased Herod,
verses.14:7: whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.
verses.14:8: And being instructed beforehand by her mother, she said, "Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
verses.14:9: And the king was grieved; yet on account of his oaths and those reclining with him at table, he commanded it to be given,
verses.14:10: and sent and had John beheaded in the prison.
verses.14:11: And his head was brought upon a platter and given to the maiden, and she carried it to her mother.
verses.14:12: And his disciples came near, took up the corpse, and buried him; then they went and brought word to Jesus.
verses.14:13: Now when Jesus heard this, He withdrew from there in a boat to a desolate place apart; and when the multitudes heard it, they followed Him on foot from the cities.
verses.14:14: And stepping out, He saw a great multitude, and He had compassion upon them and healed their sick.
verses.14:15: And when evening came, the disciples drew near to Him, saying, "The place is desolate, and the hour has already passed; dismiss the multitudes, so that they may go into the villages and buy provisions for themselves."
verses.14:16: But Jesus said to them, "They have no need to depart; you yourselves give them something to eat."
verses.14:17: Then they said to Him, "We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish."
verses.14:18: And He said, "Bring them to Me here."
verses.14:19: And having commanded the multitudes to recline upon the grass, He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up toward heaven, He blessed and broke them, and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the multitudes.
verses.14:20: And all of them ate and were satisfied, and they gathered up what was left over of the broken pieces—twelve baskets full.
verses.14:21: And those who ate were about five thousand men, apart from women and children.
verses.14:22: And immediately He compelled the disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side, until He should dismiss the multitudes.
verses.14:23: And having dismissed the multitudes, He ascended the mountain by Himself to pray. And when evening had come, He was there alone.
verses.14:24: But the boat was already in the midst of the sea, battered by the waves, for the wind was contrary.
verses.14:25: And in the fourth watch of the night He came toward them, walking upon the sea.
verses.14:26: But when the disciples saw Him walking upon the sea, they were terrified, saying, "It is a phantom!" and out of fear they cried aloud.
verses.14:27: And immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, "Take courage, it is I; do not fear."
verses.14:28: And in reply Peter said to Him, "Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You upon the waters."
verses.14:29: And He said, "Come." And stepping down from the boat, Peter walked upon the waters and came toward Jesus.
verses.14:30: Yet seeing how strong the wind was, he grew afraid, and as he began to sink, he cried aloud, saying, "Lord, save me!"
verses.14:31: And at once Jesus stretched forth His hand and grasped him, saying to him, "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"
verses.14:32: And when they climbed into the boat, the wind abated.
verses.14:33: And those in the boat worshiped Him, saying, "In truth You are the Son of God."
verses.14:34: And after crossing over, they reached the land at Gennesaret.
verses.14:35: And when the men of that place recognized Him, they sent word into all that surrounding country, and brought to Him all those who were ill,
verses.14:36: and they implored Him that they might only touch the fringe of His garment; and as many as touched it were completely healed.
verses.15:1: Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem came to Jesus, saying,
verses.15:2: "Why do Your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands whenever they eat bread."
verses.15:3: And He answered and said to them, "Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?
verses.15:4: For God commanded, saying, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'He who reviles father or mother, let him surely die.'
verses.15:5: Yet you say, 'Whoever says to his father or his mother, "Whatever you might have gained from me is a gift devoted to God,"
verses.15:6: he need not honor his father.' So you have made void the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
verses.15:7: Hypocrites! Rightly did Isaiah prophesy concerning you, saying,
verses.15:8: 'This people honors Me with their lips, yet their heart is far removed from Me;
verses.15:9: and in vain do they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the precepts of men.'"
verses.15:10: And having summoned the multitude to Himself, He said to them, "Hear and understand:
verses.15:11: it is not what enters into the mouth that defiles a man, but what proceeds out of the mouth—this defiles a man."
verses.15:12: Then the disciples came to Him and said, "Do You know that the Pharisees took offense when they heard this word?"
verses.15:13: And He answered and said, "Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted shall be uprooted.
verses.15:14: Leave them alone; they are blind guides. And if a blind man leads a blind man, both shall fall into a pit."
verses.15:15: Then Peter answered and said to Him, "Explain the parable to us."
verses.15:16: And He said, "Are you also still without understanding?
verses.15:17: Do you not yet perceive that whatever enters the mouth passes into the stomach and is cast out into the latrine?
verses.15:18: Yet the things that proceed from the mouth come forth out of the heart, and those defile a man.
verses.15:19: For out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies.
verses.15:20: These are the things that defile a man, but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a man."
verses.15:21: And departing from there, Jesus withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
verses.15:22: And behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders and cried out, saying, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is grievously afflicted by a demon."
verses.15:23: Yet He did not answer her a word. And His disciples approached and urged Him, saying, "Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us."
verses.15:24: And He answered and said, "I was not sent to any except the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
verses.15:25: Yet she approached and worshiped Him, saying, "Lord, help me!"
verses.15:26: And He answered and said, "It is not right to take the children's bread and cast it to the little dogs."
verses.15:27: And she said, "Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs eat of the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."
verses.15:28: Then Jesus answered and said to her, "O woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you desire." And her daughter was healed from that very hour.
verses.15:29: And moving on from there, Jesus came beside the Sea of Galilee, and going up onto the mountain, He sat down there.
verses.15:30: And great multitudes came to Him, bringing with them the mute, the blind, the lame, the maimed, and many others; and they laid them at His feet, and He healed them,
verses.15:31: so that the multitude marveled when they saw the mute speaking, the maimed made whole, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.
verses.15:32: Then Jesus summoned His disciples to Himself and said, "I have compassion upon the multitude, because they have remained with Me now three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not wish to send them away fasting, lest they faint along the way."
verses.15:33: And the disciples said to Him, "Where could we obtain enough loaves in a desolate place to satisfy so great a multitude?"
verses.15:34: And Jesus said to them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven, and a few small fish."
verses.15:35: And having directed the multitude to recline upon the ground,
verses.15:36: He took the seven loaves and the fish, and having given thanks, He broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.
verses.15:37: And all ate and were satisfied; and they gathered up seven large baskets full of the fragments that remained.
verses.15:38: Now those who ate were four thousand men, besides women and little children.
verses.15:39: And having dismissed the multitudes, He embarked in the boat and came into the region of Magadan.
verses.16:1: And the Pharisees and Sadducees approached, and testing Him, they asked Him to show them a sign from heaven.
verses.16:2: And He answered and said to them,
verses.16:3: ⟦"And in the morning, 'Stormy weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.' You know how to discern the face of the sky, yet you cannot discern the signs of the times.⟧
verses.16:4: An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah." And leaving them, He departed.
verses.16:5: And when the disciples came to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.
verses.16:6: And Jesus said to them, "Watch and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
verses.16:7: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, "We brought no bread."
verses.16:8: Yet Jesus, knowing this, said, "Why do you reason among yourselves, O you of little faith, because you have no bread?
verses.16:9: Do you not yet perceive, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets you gathered up?
verses.16:10: Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many large baskets you gathered up?
verses.16:11: How is it that you do not perceive that I did not speak to you concerning bread? Rather, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
verses.16:12: Then they understood that He had not told them to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
verses.16:13: Now when Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, He asked His disciples, saying, "Who do men say that the Son of Man is?"
verses.16:14: And they said, "Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and still others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
verses.16:15: He said to them, "But who do you yourselves say that I am?"
verses.16:16: And answering, Simon Peter said, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
verses.16:17: And Jesus answered and said to him, "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but My Father who is in heaven.
verses.16:18: And I Myself say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not overpower it.
verses.16:19: I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind upon the earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose upon the earth shall be loosed in heaven."
verses.16:20: Then He strictly charged the disciples that they should tell no one that He is the Christ.
verses.16:21: From that time Jesus Christ began to show to His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and on the third day be raised.
verses.16:22: And taking Him aside, Peter began to rebuke Him, saying, "Far be it from You, Lord! This shall never happen to You!"
verses.16:23: Yet He turned and said to Peter, "Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me, for you do not set your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men."
verses.16:24: Then Jesus said to His disciples, "If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me.
verses.16:25: For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it, yet whoever loses his life for My sake shall find it.
verses.16:26: For what shall a man be profited if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his own soul? Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
verses.16:27: For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will render to each one according to his conduct.
verses.16:28: Assuredly, I say to you, there are some among those standing here who shall by no means taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom."
verses.17:1: And after six days Jesus took Peter, James, and his brother John, and brought them up to a high mountain apart.
verses.17:2: And He was transfigured before them; His countenance shone like the sun, and His garments became white as the light.
verses.17:3: And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, conversing with Him.
verses.17:4: Then Peter answered Jesus and said, "Lord, it is good for us to be here; if You desire, I will make three tabernacles here—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
verses.17:5: While he was still speaking, behold, a radiant cloud overshadowed them; and behold, a voice came from the cloud, saying, "This is My Son, the Beloved, in whom I am well pleased; listen to Him."
verses.17:6: And when the disciples heard this, they fell upon their faces and were exceedingly afraid.
verses.17:7: And Jesus drew near and touched them, saying, "Rise up, and do not be afraid."
verses.17:8: And when they lifted up their eyes, they beheld no one except Jesus Himself alone.
verses.17:9: And as they were descending from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, "Tell no one the vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead."
verses.17:10: And His disciples questioned Him, saying, "Why then do the scribes declare that Elijah must come first?"
verses.17:11: And He answered and said, "Elijah indeed is coming, and he will restore all things.
verses.17:12: Yet I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they desired. In the same way, the Son of Man is also about to suffer at their hands."
verses.17:13: Then the disciples perceived that He had spoken to them concerning John the Baptist.
verses.17:14: And when they came to the multitude, a man drew near to Him, kneeling before Him
verses.17:15: and saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is afflicted with seizures and suffers terribly; for often he falls into the fire, and often into the water.
verses.17:16: And I brought him to Your disciples, yet they were not able to heal him."
verses.17:17: And Jesus answered and said, "O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I remain with you? How long shall I endure you? Bring him to Me here."
verses.17:18: And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon departed from him; and the boy was healed from that hour.
verses.17:19: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"
verses.17:20: And He said to them, "Because of your little faith; for assuredly, I say to you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain, 'Move from this place to that,' and it shall move; and nothing shall be impossible to you."
verses.17:22: Now as they were gathering together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men,
verses.17:23: and they will slay Him, and on the third day He shall be raised up." And they were deeply grieved.
verses.17:24: Now when they arrived in Capernaum, those who collected the two-drachma tax approached Peter and said, "Does your Teacher not pay the two-drachma tax?"
verses.17:25: He said, "Yes." And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, "What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect custom or tribute—from their own sons, or from strangers?"
verses.17:26: And when he said, "From strangers," Jesus said to him, "Then indeed the sons are free.
verses.17:27: Yet lest we give offense to them, go to the sea, cast in a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and when you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater. Take that and give it to them for Me and for you."
verses.18:1: In that hour the disciples approached Jesus, saying, "Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
verses.18:2: And calling a little child to Himself, He placed him in their midst
verses.18:3: and said, "Assuredly, I say to you, unless you turn and become like little children, you shall by no means enter into the kingdom of heaven.
verses.18:4: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child, he is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.18:5: And whoever welcomes one such little child in My name welcomes Me.
verses.18:6: Yet whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it is better for him that a great millstone be hung around his neck, and that he be drowned in the depths of the open sea.
verses.18:7: Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! For it is necessary that stumbling blocks come, yet woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes!
verses.18:8: Now if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it away from you; it is better for you to enter into life maimed or lame, than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.
verses.18:9: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and cast it away from you; it is better for you to enter into life with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into the fiery hell.
verses.18:10: See to it that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their angels in heaven continually behold the face of My Father who is in heaven.
verses.18:12: What do you think? If a certain man has a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine upon the mountains, and go and seek the one that is wandering?
verses.18:13: And if it comes to pass that he finds it, assuredly, I say to you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not wandered astray.
verses.18:14: Likewise, it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
verses.18:15: Now if your brother sins, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he heeds you, you have won your brother.
verses.18:16: Yet if he does not heed you, take with you one or two others, that by the mouth of two or three witnesses every matter may be established.
verses.18:17: And if he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church; and if he refuses to listen even to the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector.
verses.18:18: Assuredly, I say to you, whatever things you bind upon the earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever things you loose upon the earth shall be loosed in heaven.
verses.18:19: Again, assuredly I say to you that if two among you agree upon the earth concerning any matter that they ask, it shall be done for them by My Father who is in heaven.
verses.18:20: For where two or three are assembled in My name, there I am in their midst."
verses.18:21: Then Peter approached and said to Him, "Lord, how many times shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? As many as seven times?"
verses.18:22: Jesus said to him, "I do not say to you as many as seven times, but as many as seventy-seven times.
verses.18:23: For this reason the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who desired to settle accounts with his servants.
