verses.18:24: And when he began to settle them, one debtor was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents.
verses.18:25: Yet since he did not have the means to repay, the master commanded him to be sold, together with his wife and children and all that he possessed, and payment to be made.
verses.18:26: Therefore the servant fell down and paid homage to him, saying, 'Master, have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.'
verses.18:27: And the master of that servant, being moved with compassion, set him free and forgave him the loan.
verses.18:28: Yet when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii; and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, 'Pay back whatever you owe!'
verses.18:29: So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, saying, 'Have patience with me, and I will repay you.'
verses.18:30: Yet he was unwilling, and went away and cast him into prison until he should repay what was owed.
verses.18:31: Therefore, when his fellow servants saw what had taken place, they were deeply distressed, and came and reported to their master all that had taken place.
verses.18:32: Then his master summoned him and said to him, 'Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me.
verses.18:33: Should you not also have shown mercy to your fellow servant, even as I showed mercy to you?'
verses.18:34: And his master, being moved with wrath, delivered him to the tormentors until he should repay all that was owed to him.
verses.18:35: So also shall My heavenly Father do to you, if each one of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts."
verses.19:1: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that He departed from Galilee and came to the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.
verses.19:2: And large multitudes followed Him, and there He healed them.
verses.19:3: And Pharisees came to Him, testing Him and saying, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?"
verses.19:4: And He answered and said, "Have you not read that the One who made them from the beginning made them male and female,
verses.19:5: and said, 'For this cause a man shall leave his father and his mother and be united to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh'?
verses.19:6: Thus they are no longer two, but one flesh. What God has joined together, therefore, let no man separate."
verses.19:7: They said to Him, "Why then did Moses command to give a certificate of divorce and to send her away?"
verses.19:8: He said to them, "Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
verses.19:9: Now I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery; and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
verses.19:10: The disciples said to Him, "If such is the case of a man with his wife, it is not profitable to marry."
verses.19:11: But He said to them, "Not all can receive this word, but only those to whom it has been given.
verses.19:12: For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who is able to receive this receive it."
verses.19:13: Then little children were brought to Him so that He might lay His hands upon them and pray, but the disciples rebuked them.
verses.19:14: But Jesus said, "Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them, for to such as these belongs the kingdom of heaven."
verses.19:15: And after laying His hands upon them, He departed from there.
verses.19:16: And behold, one came to Him and said, "Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?"
verses.19:17: And He said to him, "Why do you ask Me concerning what is good? There is One who is good. Yet if you desire to enter into life, keep the commandments."
verses.19:18: He said to Him, "Which ones?" And Jesus said, "These: 'You shall not murder,' 'You shall not commit adultery,' 'You shall not steal,' 'You shall not bear false witness,'
verses.19:19: 'Honor your father and your mother,' and 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'"
verses.19:20: The young man said to Him, "All these things I have kept; what do I still lack?"
verses.19:21: Jesus said to him, "If you desire to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me."
verses.19:22: But when the young man heard that word, he departed sorrowful, for he had many possessions.
verses.19:23: Then Jesus said to His disciples, "Assuredly, I say to you that only with difficulty shall a rich man enter the kingdom of heaven.
verses.19:24: And again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."
verses.19:25: When the disciples heard this, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, "Who then can be saved?"
verses.19:26: But Jesus looked upon them and said to them, "With men this is impossible, yet with God all things are possible."
verses.19:27: Then Peter answered and said to Him, "Behold, we have forsaken all things and followed You. What then shall there be for us?"
verses.19:28: And Jesus said to them, "Assuredly, I say to you that in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits upon the throne of His glory, you who have followed Me shall also sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.19:29: And everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, for the sake of My name, shall receive a hundredfold and shall inherit eternal life.
verses.19:30: Yet many who are first shall be last, and the last first."
verses.20:1: "For the kingdom of heaven is like a master of a house who went out early at dawn to hire laborers for his vineyard.
verses.20:2: And when he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
verses.20:3: And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
verses.20:4: and he said to those men, 'Go into the vineyard as well, and whatever is just I will give you.'
verses.20:5: So they went. Going out again about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did likewise.
verses.20:6: And about the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and said to them, 'Why have you stood here all the day idle?'
verses.20:7: They said to him, 'Because no one hired us.' He said to them, 'You also go into the vineyard.'
verses.20:8: Now when evening had come, the master of the vineyard said to his steward, 'Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last to the first.'
verses.20:9: And when those hired about the eleventh hour came, each received a denarius.
verses.20:10: And when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; yet they also each received a denarius.
verses.20:11: And when they had received it, they murmured against the master of the house,
verses.20:12: saying, 'These last worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.'
verses.20:13: But answering one of them, he said, 'Friend, I am not wronging you. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?
verses.20:14: Take what belongs to you and go your way. I choose to give to this last man the same as to you.
verses.20:15: Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with what is mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?'
verses.20:16: Thus the last shall be first, and the first last."
verses.20:17: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside privately, and on the road He said to them,
verses.20:18: "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes, and they shall condemn Him to death,
verses.20:19: and they shall deliver Him over to the Gentiles to mock and to scourge and to crucify; and on the third day He shall rise again."
verses.20:20: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to Him with her sons, kneeling down before Him and asking something from Him.
verses.20:21: And He said to her, "What do you desire?" She said to Him, "Command that these two sons of mine may sit, one at Your right hand and one at Your left, in Your kingdom."
verses.20:22: But Jesus answered and said, "You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?" They said to Him, "We are able."
verses.20:23: He said to them, "My cup indeed you shall drink; yet to sit at My right hand and at the left is not Mine to grant, but it belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by My Father."
verses.20:24: And when the ten heard it, they were indignant concerning the two brothers.
verses.20:25: But Jesus summoned them to Himself and said, "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and the great ones wield authority over them.
verses.20:26: It shall not be so among you; rather, whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant,
verses.20:27: and whoever desires to be first among you shall be your slave—
verses.20:28: even as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many."
verses.20:29: And as they were going out from Jericho, a great multitude followed Him.
verses.20:30: And behold, two blind men sitting beside the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"
verses.20:31: And the multitude rebuked them that they should be silent; yet they cried out all the more, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"
verses.20:32: And Jesus stood still, called them, and said, "What do you desire Me to do for you?"
verses.20:33: They said to Him, "Lord, that our eyes may be opened."
verses.20:34: And moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes; and immediately they regained their sight and followed Him.
verses.21:1: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, by the Mount of Olives, Jesus then sent forth two disciples,
verses.21:2: saying to them, "Go into the village across from you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her; untie them and lead them to Me.
verses.21:3: And if anyone says anything to you, you shall say, 'The Lord has need of them,' and he will send them at once."
verses.21:4: Now this took place that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
verses.21:5: "Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Behold, your King comes to you, meek and mounted upon a donkey, and upon a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.'"
verses.21:6: So the disciples went and did just as Jesus had instructed them;
verses.21:7: they brought the donkey and the colt, placed their garments on them, and He sat upon them.
verses.21:8: And a very great multitude spread their own garments on the road, while others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them in the way.
verses.21:9: And the multitudes going before Him and those following cried out, saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
verses.21:10: And when He entered Jerusalem, the entire city was shaken, saying, "Who is this?"
verses.21:11: And the multitudes were saying, "This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee."
verses.21:12: And Jesus went into the temple and cast out all those selling and buying in the temple, and He overturned the tables of the moneychangers and the seats of those selling doves.
verses.21:13: And He said to them, "It is written, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer,' yet you are making it a den of robbers."
verses.21:14: And the blind and the lame approached Him in the temple, and He healed them.
verses.21:15: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wondrous things that He did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" they were indignant,
verses.21:16: and they said to Him, "Do You hear what these are saying?" And Jesus said to them, "Yes. Have you never read, 'Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babes You have prepared praise'?"
verses.21:17: And leaving them, He went out of the city to Bethany, and lodged there.
verses.21:18: Now early in the morning, as He was returning to the city, He became hungry.
verses.21:19: And seeing a lone fig tree beside the road, He went up to it and found nothing on it except leaves only; and He said to it, "Never again shall fruit come from you forever." And the fig tree withered instantly.
verses.21:20: And when the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, "How did the fig tree wither instantly?"
verses.21:21: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Assuredly, I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and cast into the sea,' it shall be done.
verses.21:22: And all things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you shall receive."
verses.21:23: Now when He came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached Him as He was teaching, saying, "By what authority are You doing these things? And who gave You this authority?"
verses.21:24: And Jesus answered and said to them, "I also will ask you one thing; if you tell Me that, I too will tell you by what authority I do these things:
verses.21:25: The baptism of John—where was it from? From heaven or from men?" And they reasoned among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
verses.21:26: But if we say, 'From men,' we fear the multitude, for all hold John to be a prophet."
verses.21:27: So they answered Jesus and said, "We do not know." And He Himself said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
verses.21:28: But what do you think? A man had two sons; and coming to the first, he said, 'Son, go work today in the vineyard.'
verses.21:29: And he answered and said, 'I will not,' yet afterward he relented and went.
verses.21:30: Then he came to the other and spoke in the same manner; and he answered and said, 'I will, sir,' yet he did not go.
verses.21:31: Which of the two did the will of the father?" They said, "The first." Jesus said to them, "Assuredly, I say to you that the tax collectors and the harlots go ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
verses.21:32: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, whereas the tax collectors and the harlots believed him; and when you saw it, you did not afterward relent so as to believe him.
verses.21:33: Hear another parable: There was a householder who planted a vineyard, and set a hedge around it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower; and he leased it to vinedressers and departed on a journey.
verses.21:34: Now when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the vinedressers to receive his fruits.
verses.21:35: And the vinedressers seized his servants, and beat one, slew another, and stoned another.
verses.21:36: Again he sent other servants, more than the first, and they treated them in the same manner.
verses.21:37: At last he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
verses.21:38: But when the vinedressers saw the son, they said among themselves, 'This is the heir. Come, let us slay him and possess his inheritance.'
verses.21:39: So they seized him, cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.
verses.21:40: Therefore, when the master of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those vinedressers?"
verses.21:41: They said to Him, "He will bring those wretches to a wretched end, and will lease out the vineyard to other vinedressers who will render to him the fruits in their seasons."
verses.21:42: Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures, 'The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner; this came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?
verses.21:43: Therefore I say to you that the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation bringing forth its fruits.
verses.21:44: And the one who falls upon this stone shall be shattered; yet on whomever it falls, it will crush him to dust."
verses.21:45: Now when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard His parables, they perceived that He was speaking about them.
verses.21:46: And although they sought to seize Him, they feared the multitudes, because they regarded Him as a prophet.
verses.22:1: And answering, Jesus spoke to them again in parables, saying,
verses.22:2: "The kingdom of heaven is likened to a certain king who gave a wedding feast for his son.
verses.22:3: And he sent forth his servants to summon those who had been invited to the wedding feast, yet they were unwilling to come.
verses.22:4: Again he sent forth other servants, saying, 'Tell those who have been invited, "Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and the fattened cattle have been slain, and all things are ready. Come to the wedding feast."'
verses.22:5: But paying no heed, they went away, one to his own farm, and another to his trade.
verses.22:6: And the rest laid hold of his servants, treated them shamefully, and put them to death.
verses.22:7: Then the king was filled with wrath; and sending forth his armies, he destroyed those murderers and set their city on fire.
verses.22:8: Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding feast indeed is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.
verses.22:9: Go therefore to the main thoroughfares, and as many as you may find, invite to the wedding feast.'
verses.22:10: So those servants went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both evil and good; and the wedding hall became full of guests.
verses.22:11: Now when the king entered to look upon the guests, he saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment.
verses.22:12: And he said to him, 'Friend, how did you enter here without having a wedding garment?' And he was rendered speechless.
verses.22:13: Then the king said to the attendants, 'Bind his feet and hands and cast him out into the outer darkness; in that place there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
verses.22:14: For many are summoned, yet few are chosen."
verses.22:15: Then the Pharisees went out and took counsel together as to how they might ensnare Him in speech.
verses.22:16: And they sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and You defer to no one; for You do not look upon the outward appearance of men.
verses.22:17: Tell us, therefore, what do You think? Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?"
verses.22:18: But Jesus, knowing their malice, said, "Why are you putting Me to the test, you hypocrites?
verses.22:19: Show Me the coin used for the tribute." And they brought Him a denarius.
verses.22:20: And He said to them, "Whose is this image and inscription?"
verses.22:21: They said, "Caesar's." Then He said to them, "Render therefore to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God."
verses.22:22: And upon hearing this, they marveled; and leaving Him, they departed.
verses.22:23: On that day some Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, approached Him and questioned Him,
verses.22:24: saying, "Teacher, Moses declared, 'If any man dies having no children, his brother shall take his wife in marriage and raise up offspring for his brother.'
verses.22:25: Now there were among us seven brothers. And the first married and died, and having no offspring, he left his wife to his brother;
verses.22:26: in like manner also the second and the third, down to all seven.
verses.22:27: And last of all, the woman died.
verses.22:28: In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife among the seven shall she be? For all of them had her."
verses.22:29: But answering, Jesus said to them, "You are in error, knowing neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
verses.22:30: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, rather they are as angels in heaven.
verses.22:31: Yet regarding the resurrection of the dead, have you not read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
verses.22:32: 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? He is not the God of the dead, rather of the living."
verses.22:33: And when the multitudes heard this, they were astounded at His teaching.
verses.22:34: Now when the Pharisees heard that He had silenced the Sadducees, they assembled together in one place.
verses.22:35: And one of them, an expert in the law, questioned Him, testing Him:
verses.22:36: "Teacher, which commandment is greatest in the law?"
verses.22:37: And He said to him, "You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole mind.
verses.22:38: This is the greatest and foremost commandment.
verses.22:39: And a second is similar to it: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'
verses.22:40: Upon these two commandments the whole law hangs, and the prophets."
verses.22:41: Now while the Pharisees were assembled together, Jesus questioned them,
verses.22:42: saying, "What do you think concerning the Christ? Whose son is He?" They said to Him, "David's."
verses.22:43: He said to them, "How then does David in the Spirit call Him Lord, saying,
verses.22:44: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand, until I place Your enemies beneath Your feet"'?
verses.22:45: If therefore David calls Him Lord, how is He his son?"
verses.22:46: And no one was able to answer Him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day forward to question Him any longer.
verses.23:1: Then Jesus addressed the multitudes and His disciples,
verses.23:2: saying, "Upon the seat of Moses the scribes and the Pharisees sit.
verses.23:3: Therefore, all that they tell you, do and keep; yet do not act according to their works, for they speak, and do not do.
verses.23:4: And they bind burdens heavy and difficult to bear, and place them upon the shoulders of men; yet they themselves are unwilling to move them with their finger.
verses.23:5: Moreover, all their works they perform so as to be seen by men; for they widen their phylacteries and enlarge the tassels,
verses.23:6: and they love the place of honor at feasts and the foremost seats in the synagogues,
verses.23:7: and salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called 'Rabbi' by men.
verses.23:8: But as for you, do not be called 'Rabbi,' for One is your Instructor, and all of you are brethren.
verses.23:9: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for One is your heavenly Father.
verses.23:10: And do not let yourselves be called instructors, because your Instructor is One—the Christ.
verses.23:11: Yet the greatest among you shall be your servant.
verses.23:12: And everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself shall be exalted.
verses.23:13: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven before men; for you do not enter yourselves, nor do you permit those who are entering to enter.
verses.23:15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you traverse the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as yourselves.
verses.23:16: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; yet whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound.'
verses.23:17: You foolish and blind! For which is greater, the gold, or the temple that has sanctified the gold?
verses.23:18: And, 'Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; yet whoever swears by the gift upon it is bound.'
verses.23:19: You foolish and blind! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
verses.23:20: Therefore, the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by all things upon it;
verses.23:21: and the one who swears by the temple swears by it and by Him who dwells in it;
verses.23:22: and the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by Him who sits upon it.
verses.23:23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law—justice and mercy and faithfulness. Yet these you ought to have practiced, without neglecting the others.
verses.23:24: Blind guides, who strain out the gnat, yet swallow the camel!
verses.23:25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, yet within they are full of robbery and self-indulgence.
verses.23:26: You blind Pharisee, first cleanse the inside of the cup and of the dish, so that the outside of them may also become clean.
verses.23:27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you resemble whitewashed tombs, which outwardly indeed appear fair, yet inwardly are full of the bones of the dead and all uncleanness;
verses.23:28: in like manner you also outwardly appear righteous to men, yet inwardly you are filled with hypocrisy and lawlessness.
verses.23:29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you construct the tombs of the prophets and adorn the memorials of the righteous,
verses.23:30: and say, 'If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the prophets.'
verses.23:31: Thus you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
verses.23:32: And you yourselves, fill up the measure of your fathers!
verses.23:33: Serpents, offspring of vipers! How shall you escape from the judgment of hell?
verses.23:34: For this reason, behold, I am sending to you prophets, wise men, and scribes: some of them you will slay and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
verses.23:35: so that upon you may come all the righteous blood poured out upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah, son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
verses.23:36: Assuredly, I tell you, all these things shall come upon this generation.
verses.23:37: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, she who slays the prophets and stones those who have been sent to her—how often I desired to gather your children together, even as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
verses.23:38: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
verses.23:39: For I tell you, from this time forward you shall by no means see Me until you say, 'Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!'"
verses.24:1: And Jesus went out from the temple and was going on His way, and His disciples came to Him to point out to Him the buildings of the temple.
verses.24:2: But He answered and said to them, "Do you not see all these things? Assuredly, I say to you, not one stone shall by any means be left here upon another that shall not be cast down."
verses.24:3: Now as He was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, "Tell us, when shall these things be, and what shall be the sign of Your coming and of the consummation of the age?"
verses.24:4: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Take heed lest anyone lead you astray.
verses.24:5: For many shall come in My name, saying, 'I am the Christ,' and shall lead many astray.
verses.24:6: And you shall hear of wars and reports of wars; see that you are not alarmed, for this must come to pass, yet the end is not yet.
verses.24:7: For nation shall rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there shall be famines and earthquakes in various places.
verses.24:8: Now all these things are the beginning of birth pangs.
verses.24:9: Then they shall deliver you over to tribulation and put you to death, and you shall be hated by all the nations on account of My name.
verses.24:10: And then many shall fall away, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.
verses.24:11: And many false prophets shall arise and lead many astray.
verses.24:12: And because lawlessness shall be multiplied, the love of the many shall grow cold.
verses.24:13: Yet he who endures to the end, the same shall be saved.
verses.24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be proclaimed throughout the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end shall come.
verses.24:15: Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),
verses.24:16: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains;
verses.24:17: let him who is on the housetop not come down to take away the things out of his house;
verses.24:18: and let him who is in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
verses.24:19: And woe to those who are with child and to those who are nursing in those days!
verses.24:20: And pray that your flight may not be in winter nor on a Sabbath;
verses.24:21: for then there shall be great tribulation, such as has not come to pass from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever shall be.
verses.24:22: And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would have been saved; yet for the sake of the elect those days shall be cut short.
verses.24:23: Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is the Christ!' or 'Here!' do not believe it.
verses.24:24: For false christs and false prophets shall arise and perform great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect.
verses.24:25: Behold, I have told you beforehand.
verses.24:26: Therefore if they say to you, 'Behold, He is in the wilderness!' do not go forth; 'Behold, He is in the inner chambers!' do not believe it.
verses.24:27: For just as the lightning flashes forth from the east and shines even to the west, so shall the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.24:28: Wherever the carcass is, there the vultures shall be gathered together.
verses.24:29: And immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give its radiance, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.
verses.24:30: And then the sign of the Son of Man shall appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth shall mourn, and they shall behold the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
verses.24:31: And He shall send forth His angels with a loud trumpet, and they shall gather together His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
verses.24:32: Now learn the parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch has become tender and puts forth its leaves, you know that summer is near.
verses.24:33: Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that He is near, right at the doors.
verses.24:34: Assuredly, I say to you, this generation shall by no means pass away until all these things have come to pass.
verses.24:35: Heaven and earth shall pass away, yet My words shall never pass away.
verses.24:36: Now concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels of the heavens nor the Son, except the Father alone.
verses.24:37: For just as the days of Noah were, so shall the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.24:38: For as they were in those days before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark,
verses.24:39: and they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away—so also shall the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.24:40: Then two men shall be in the field: one is taken, and one is left;
verses.24:41: two women shall be grinding at the mill: one is taken, and one is left.
verses.24:42: Keep watch therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
verses.24:43: Now know this: if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have permitted his house to be broken into.
verses.24:44: For this reason you also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour that you do not expect.
verses.24:45: Who then is the faithful and prudent servant, whom the master has set over his household, to give them their food in due season?
verses.24:46: Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, shall find doing so.
verses.24:47: Assuredly, I say to you, he shall set him over all his possessions.
verses.24:48: Yet if that wicked servant says in his heart, 'My master delays,'
verses.24:49: and begins to strike his fellow servants, and eats and drinks with the drunkards,
verses.24:50: the master of that servant shall come on a day when he does not expect him, and at an hour that he does not know,
verses.24:51: and shall cut him in two and appoint his portion with the hypocrites; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
verses.25:1: "Then the kingdom of heaven shall be compared to ten virgins, who, taking their lamps, went forth to meet the bridegroom.
verses.25:2: Now five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
verses.25:3: For the foolish ones, taking their lamps, did not take oil with them;
verses.25:4: but the wise ones took oil in vessels along with their lamps.
verses.25:5: Now as the bridegroom tarried, all of them grew drowsy and slept.
verses.25:6: And at midnight a cry rang out: 'Behold, the bridegroom! Go forth to meet him!'
verses.25:7: Then all those virgins rose up and trimmed their lamps.
verses.25:8: And the foolish ones said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.'
verses.25:9: But the wise answered, saying, 'Lest there should not be enough for both us and you, go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.'
verses.25:10: And while they went away to buy, the bridegroom came; and those who were ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
verses.25:11: Afterward the remaining virgins also came, saying, 'Lord, Lord, open to us!'
verses.25:12: But he replied and said, 'Assuredly, I say to you, I do not know you.'
verses.25:13: Keep watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.
verses.25:14: For it is just as when a man going on a journey summoned his own servants and entrusted his possessions to them.
verses.25:15: To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability; and he departed on his journey.
verses.25:16: Immediately he who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and gained five more talents.
verses.25:17: In the same manner, he also who had the two gained two more.
verses.25:18: But he who had received the one went away, dug in the earth, and hid the money of his master.
verses.25:19: Now after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
verses.25:20: And he who had received the five talents came forward and brought five more talents, saying, 'Master, you entrusted five talents to me; behold, I have gained five more talents.'
verses.25:21: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful over a few things; I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your master.'
verses.25:22: He also who had the two talents came forward and said, 'Master, you entrusted two talents to me; behold, I have gained two more talents.'
verses.25:23: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful over a few things; I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your master.'
verses.25:24: Then he also who had received the one talent came forward and said, 'Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow, and gathering from where you did not scatter;
verses.25:25: and being afraid, I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Behold, you have what is yours.'
verses.25:26: But his master answered and said to him, 'You wicked and slothful servant, you knew that I reap where I did not sow, and gather from where I did not scatter?
verses.25:27: Therefore you ought to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I would have received back my own with interest.
verses.25:28: Take the talent from him therefore, and give it to him who has the ten talents.
verses.25:29: For to everyone who has, more shall be given, and he shall have an abundance; but from him who does not have, even what he has shall be taken away from him.
verses.25:30: And cast the worthless servant into the outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
verses.25:31: Now when the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He shall sit upon the throne of His glory.
verses.25:32: And before Him all the nations shall be gathered, and He shall separate them one from another, just as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,
verses.25:33: and He shall place the sheep on His right hand, but the goats on the left.
verses.25:34: Then the King shall say to those at His right hand, 'Come, you who are blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:
verses.25:35: for I was hungry and you gave Me food to eat; I was thirsty and you gave Me drink; I was a stranger and you welcomed Me in;
verses.25:36: naked, and you clothed Me; I was sick and you visited Me; I was in prison and you came to Me.'
verses.25:37: Then the righteous shall answer Him, saying, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You drink?
verses.25:38: And when did we see You a stranger and welcome You in, or naked and clothe You?
verses.25:39: And when did we see You sick, or in prison, and come to You?'
verses.25:40: And answering, the King shall say to them, 'Assuredly, I say to you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me.'
verses.25:41: Then He shall say also to those on the left, 'Depart from Me, you accursed ones, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels:
verses.25:42: for I was hungry and you gave Me no food to eat; I was thirsty and you gave Me no drink;
verses.25:43: I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me in; naked, and you did not clothe Me; sick and in prison, and you did not visit Me.'
verses.25:44: Then they also shall answer, saying, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to You?'
verses.25:45: Then He shall answer them, saying, 'Assuredly, I say to you, insofar as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.'
verses.25:46: And these shall go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life."
verses.26:1: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these words, He said to His disciples,
verses.26:2: "You know that after two days the Passover comes, and the Son of Man is delivered up to be crucified."
verses.26:3: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered together in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,
verses.26:4: and took counsel together that they might seize Jesus by deceit and put Him to death.
verses.26:5: But they were saying, "Not during the feast, lest an uproar arise among the people."
verses.26:6: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
verses.26:7: a woman came to Him holding an alabaster flask of very precious ointment, and she poured it upon His head as He reclined at table.
verses.26:8: But when the disciples saw it, they were indignant, saying, "For what purpose is this waste?
verses.26:9: For this could have been sold for a great sum and given to the poor."
verses.26:10: But Jesus, perceiving this, said to them, "Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a noble work for Me.
verses.26:11: For the poor you always have with you, but Me you do not always have.
verses.26:12: For in pouring this ointment upon My body, she did so to prepare Me for burial.
verses.26:13: Assuredly, I say to you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what she has done shall also be spoken of as a memorial for her."
verses.26:14: Then one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
verses.26:15: and said, "What are you willing to give me, and I will deliver Him to you?" And they weighed out to him thirty pieces of silver.
verses.26:16: And from that time on he kept seeking an opportunity to betray Him.
verses.26:17: Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying, "Where do You wish us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?"
verses.26:18: And He said, "Go into the city to a certain man, and say to him, 'The Teacher says: My time is near; at your house I will keep the Passover with My disciples.'"
verses.26:19: And the disciples did just as Jesus had instructed them, and they made ready the Passover.
verses.26:20: Now when evening had come, He reclined at table with the twelve.
verses.26:21: And while they were eating, He said, "Assuredly, I say to you that one of you shall betray Me."
verses.26:22: And deeply grieved, each one of them began to say to Him, "Surely it is not I, Lord?"
verses.26:23: And He answered and said, "The one who has dipped his hand with Me in the dish, that one shall betray Me.
verses.26:24: The Son of Man indeed goes away just as it is written concerning Him, yet woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born."
verses.26:25: Then Judas, who was betraying Him, answered and said, "Surely it is not I, Rabbi?" He said to him, "You have said so."
verses.26:26: Now while they were eating, Jesus took bread, and after blessing it, He broke it and gave it to the disciples, saying, "Take, eat; this is My body."
verses.26:27: And taking a cup, and having given thanks, He gave it to them, saying, "Drink from it, all of you,
verses.26:28: for this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out on behalf of many for the forgiveness of sins.
verses.26:29: Yet I say to you, from now on I shall by no means drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of My Father."
verses.26:30: And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
verses.26:31: Then Jesus said to them, "All of you shall stumble on account of Me this night, for it is written: 'I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered.'
verses.26:32: Yet after I have been raised, I will go before you into Galilee."
verses.26:33: But Peter answered and said to Him, "Though all stumble on account of You, I will never stumble."
verses.26:34: Jesus said to him, "Assuredly, I say to you that during this night, before a rooster crows, you shall deny Me three times."
verses.26:35: Peter said to Him, "Even if I must die with You, I will by no means deny You." And all the disciples spoke likewise.
verses.26:36: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and He said to the disciples, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
verses.26:37: And taking with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, He began to be grieved and in deep anguish.
verses.26:38: Then He said to them, "My soul is deeply grieved, even to death; remain here and keep watch with Me."
verses.26:39: And advancing a little farther, He fell upon His face, praying and saying, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from Me; yet not as I will, but as You will."
verses.26:40: And He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and He said to Peter, "Were you not able then to keep watch with Me for one hour?
verses.26:41: Keep watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is eager, yet the flesh is weak."
verses.26:42: Again, a second time, He went away and prayed, saying, "My Father, if this cannot pass away unless I drink it, let Your will be done."
verses.26:43: And coming again, He found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down.
verses.26:44: And leaving them again, He went away and prayed a third time, speaking the same word once more.
verses.26:45: Then He came to the disciples and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and taking your rest? Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is delivered up into the hands of sinners.
verses.26:46: Arise, let us go! Behold, the one who betrays Me has drawn near."
verses.26:47: And while He was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders of the people.
verses.26:48: Now the one betraying Him had given them a sign, saying, "Whomever I kiss, He is the one; seize Him."
verses.26:49: And immediately approaching Jesus, he said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and kissed Him.
verses.26:50: But Jesus said to him, "Friend, do that for which you have come." Then they came forward, laid hands upon Jesus, and seized Him.
verses.26:51: And behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
verses.26:52: Then Jesus said to him, "Return your sword to its place, for all who take up the sword shall perish by the sword.
verses.26:53: Or do you suppose that I cannot appeal to My Father, and He will at once provide Me with more than twelve legions of angels?
verses.26:54: How then should the Scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must come to pass?"
verses.26:55: In that hour Jesus said to the multitudes, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to capture Me? Day after day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me.
verses.26:56: Yet all this has come to pass that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples abandoned Him and fled.
verses.26:57: Now those who had seized Jesus led Him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.
verses.26:58: But Peter followed Him from a distance as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and going inside, he sat with the officers to see the outcome.
verses.26:59: Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might put Him to death,
verses.26:60: yet they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. At last, however, two came forward
verses.26:61: and said, "This man declared, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it in three days.'"
verses.26:62: And the high priest arose and said to Him, "Do You make no answer? What is it that these men testify against You?"
verses.26:63: But Jesus remained silent. And the high priest said to Him, "I put You under oath by the living God that You tell us whether You are the Christ, the Son of God."
verses.26:64: Jesus said to him, "You have said so. Moreover, I say to you, from now on you shall see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power, and coming upon the clouds of heaven."
verses.26:65: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, "He has spoken blasphemy! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy!
verses.26:66: What is your judgment?" And they answered and said, "He is worthy of death."
verses.26:67: Then they spat in His face and struck Him with their fists, while others slapped Him,
verses.26:68: saying, "Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is the one who struck You?"
verses.26:69: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. And a servant girl came up to him, saying, "You also were with Jesus the Galilean."
verses.26:70: But he denied it before them all, saying, "I do not know what you are saying."
verses.26:71: And when he had gone out to the gateway, another girl saw him and said to those who were there, "This man was with Jesus the Nazarene."
verses.26:72: And again he denied it with an oath, "I do not know the man!"
verses.26:73: And after a little while those who were standing by came up and said to Peter, "Truly you also are one of them, for indeed your speech gives you away."
verses.26:74: Then he began to curse and to swear, "I do not know the man!" And immediately a rooster crowed.
verses.26:75: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said, "Before a rooster crows, you shall deny Me three times." And going outside, he wept bitterly.
verses.27:1: Now when morning had arrived, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel together against Jesus so that they might put Him to death.
verses.27:2: And having bound Him, they led Him away and delivered Him over to Pilate the governor.
verses.27:3: Then Judas, the one who had betrayed Him, seeing that He was condemned, was seized with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
verses.27:4: saying, "I have sinned in betraying innocent blood." And they said, "What is that to us? You see to it!"
verses.27:5: And casting down the pieces of silver into the sanctuary, he departed; and going away, he hanged himself.
verses.27:6: Now the chief priests, taking the pieces of silver, said, "It is not lawful to cast them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood."
verses.27:7: And having taken counsel together, they purchased with them the Potter's Field as a burial place for strangers.
verses.27:8: Therefore that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
verses.27:9: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of Him who was valued, on whom some of the sons of Israel set a price,
verses.27:10: and they gave them for the potter's field, just as the Lord directed me."
verses.27:11: Now Jesus stood before the governor; and the governor questioned Him, saying, "Are You the King of the Jews?" And Jesus said to him, "You say so."
verses.27:12: And as He was being accused by the chief priests and elders, He made no answer.
verses.27:13: Then Pilate said to Him, "Do You not hear how many things they witness against You?"
verses.27:14: Yet He gave him no answer, not even to a single word, so that the governor marveled exceedingly.
verses.27:15: Now at each feast the governor was accustomed to release to the multitude one prisoner whom they wished.
verses.27:16: And at that time they held a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.
verses.27:17: Therefore, when they had gathered together, Pilate said to them, "Whom do you wish that I release to you—Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"
verses.27:18: For he knew that out of envy they had delivered Him up.
verses.27:19: Now while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent word to him, saying, "Have nothing to do with that righteous Man, for I have suffered many things this day in a dream on account of Him."
verses.27:20: But the chief priests and the elders convinced the multitudes that they should demand Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
verses.27:21: Then the governor answered and said to them, "Which of the two do you wish me to release to you?" And they said, "Barabbas."
verses.27:22: Pilate said to them, "Then what shall I do with Jesus, the one called Christ?" All of them said, "Let Him be crucified!"
verses.27:23: And he replied, "Why, what evil has He done?" Yet they kept crying out all the more, saying, "Let Him be crucified!"
verses.27:24: Now when Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather that an uproar was rising, he took water and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, "I am innocent of this blood; you yourselves see to it."
verses.27:25: And in answer, all the people said, "His blood be upon us and upon our children!"
verses.27:26: Then he released Barabbas to them; and having scourged Jesus, he delivered Him over to be crucified.
verses.27:27: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the Praetorium and assembled the whole cohort around Him.
verses.27:28: And having stripped Him, they put a scarlet cloak around Him,
verses.27:29: and having woven a crown of thorns, they placed it upon His head, and a reed in His right hand; and kneeling before Him, they mocked Him, saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
verses.27:30: And spitting upon Him, they took the reed and kept striking Him upon the head.
verses.27:31: And when they had mocked Him, they stripped Him of the cloak, clothed Him with His own garments, and led Him away to crucify Him.
verses.27:32: Now as they were going out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name; him they pressed into service to bear His cross.
verses.27:33: And having come to a place called Golgotha, which is called Place of a Skull,
verses.27:34: they gave Him wine mingled with gall to drink; yet when He had tasted it, He was unwilling to drink.
verses.27:35: And having crucified Him, they divided His garments among themselves by casting lots,
verses.27:36: and sitting down, they kept guard over Him there.
verses.27:37: And they placed above His head the written charge against Him: "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
verses.27:38: At that time two robbers were crucified along with Him, one on the right hand and one on the left.
verses.27:39: And those who were passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads
verses.27:40: and saying, "You who tear down the sanctuary and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross."
verses.27:41: Likewise the chief priests also, mocking along with the scribes and elders, said,
verses.27:42: "He saved others, yet He cannot save Himself! He is the King of Israel; let Him now come down from the cross, and we will believe in Him.
verses.27:43: He has placed His trust in God; let Him rescue Him now if He delights in Him, for He said, 'I am the Son of God.'"
verses.27:44: And in the same manner the robbers also, who were crucified with Him, reproached Him.
verses.27:45: Now from the sixth hour, darkness fell upon all the land until the ninth hour.
verses.27:46: And about the ninth hour, Jesus cried aloud with a great voice, saying, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"—which means, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"
verses.27:47: Now certain ones of those who were standing there, hearing this, were saying, "This Man is calling Elijah."
verses.27:48: And at once one of them ran, and taking a sponge and filling it with sour wine, he placed it upon a reed and gave it to Him to drink.
verses.27:49: But the others said, "Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to save Him."
verses.27:50: And Jesus, crying out once more with a great voice, yielded up His spirit.
verses.27:51: And behold, the veil of the sanctuary was torn from top to bottom in two; and the earth shook, and the rocks were split apart,
verses.27:52: and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised up,
verses.27:53: and coming forth from the tombs after His resurrection, they entered into the holy city and appeared to many.
verses.27:54: Now the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus, upon seeing the earthquake and the things that had happened, feared exceedingly, saying, "Truly this Man was the Son of God!"
verses.27:55: And many women were there, looking on from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to Him;
verses.27:56: among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
verses.27:57: And when evening arrived, a wealthy man from Arimathea came, Joseph by name, who had himself also become a disciple of Jesus.
verses.27:58: This man approached Pilate and requested the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be handed over.
verses.27:59: And taking the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen shroud,
verses.27:60: and placed it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock; and having rolled a great stone to the doorway of the tomb, he departed.
verses.27:61: And Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, seated facing the tomb.
verses.27:62: Now on the next day, which is the day after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered together before Pilate,
verses.27:63: saying, "Sir, we have remembered how that deceiver said while He was still alive, 'After three days I will rise.'
verses.27:64: Therefore command that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest His disciples come and steal Him away and say to the people, 'He has been raised from the dead,' and the last deception will be worse than the first."
verses.27:65: Then Pilate said to them, "You have a guard; go, make it secure as you know how."
verses.27:66: So they went and made the tomb secure with the guard, sealing the stone.
verses.28:1: Now after the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to view the sepulcher.
verses.28:2: And behold, a great earthquake occurred; for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and approached, rolled away the stone, and was sitting upon it.
verses.28:3: Now his countenance was like lightning, and his garment was white as snow.
verses.28:4: And from fear of him, those keeping watch were shaken and became as dead men.
verses.28:5: Then the angel answered and said to the women, "As for you, do not be afraid; for I know that you are seeking Jesus, who has been crucified.
verses.28:6: He is not here, for He has been raised, just as He said. Come, behold the place where He lay.
verses.28:7: And go swiftly and tell His disciples, 'He has been raised from the dead; and behold, He is going before you into Galilee; there you shall see Him.' Behold, I have told you."
verses.28:8: And departing swiftly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to report to His disciples.
verses.28:9: And behold, Jesus met them, saying, "Rejoice!" And drawing near, they clasped His feet and worshiped Him.
verses.28:10: Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go, report to My brethren that they should depart into Galilee, and there they shall see Me."
verses.28:11: Now while they were on their way, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had come to pass.
verses.28:12: And having assembled with the elders and taken counsel together, they gave a substantial sum of silver to the soldiers,
verses.28:13: saying, "Say, 'His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we were sleeping.'
verses.28:14: And if this should come before the governor, we ourselves will persuade him and keep you free from care."
verses.28:15: So they received the silver and did as they were taught. And this report has been spread abroad among the Jews until this very day.
verses.28:16: Now the eleven disciples departed into Galilee, to the mountain that Jesus had designated for them,
verses.28:17: and when they saw Him, they worshiped, yet some doubted.
verses.28:18: And drawing near, Jesus spoke to them, saying, "All authority in heaven and upon the earth has been given to Me.
verses.28:19: Therefore, go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,
verses.28:20: teaching them to keep all things that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you all the days, even until the close of the age."

notes.1:1: The Greek word genesis means "origin," "birth," or "lineage," echoing the Septuagint of Genesis 2:4 and 5:1.
notes.1:7: The Greek critical text reads "Asaph" (rather than "Asa," the king of Judah in 1 Kings 15:8), a spelling attested in the earliest manuscripts of Matthew.
notes.1:10: The Greek critical text reads "Amos" (rather than "Amon," the king of Judah in 2 Kings 21:18), reflecting the earliest manuscript tradition of Matthew.
notes.1:25: The Greek critical text reads simply "a Son"; later Byzantine manuscripts expand this to "her firstborn Son."
notes.2:1: Greek magoi refers to eastern sages, scholars, or astrologers, traditionally rendered "wise men."
notes.2:2: The Greek phrase en te anatole can mean either "in the east" or, in astronomical usage, "at its rising."
notes.2:18: The Greek critical text reads "weeping and great mourning," omitting "lamentation," which later manuscripts added to harmonize with the Septuagint of Jeremiah 31:15.
notes.2:23: No single Old Testament verse contains these exact words; Matthew summarizes a prophetic theme often linked to the Hebrew word netser ("branch," Isaiah 11:1) or to the humble obscurity of Nazareth.
notes.3:11: The Greek preposition en may be rendered "with" or "in"; baptism "with the Holy Spirit and fire" denotes both purifying renewal and eschatological judgment.
notes.3:15: "Fulfill all righteousness" refers to Jesus' complete obedience to God's redemptive will and His solidarity with those He came to save.
notes.3:16: The Greek critical text reads "the heavens were opened" without the words "to Him" found in later manuscripts.
notes.4:10: The critical Greek text reads simply "Depart, Satan" (Hypage, Satana); later manuscripts add "behind Me" (opiso mou), likely assimilated from Matthew 16:23.
notes.4:12: The Greek verb paredothe ("was delivered up" or "handed over") refers to John's arrest and imprisonment, using the same term Matthew later applies to the handing over of Jesus. Early Greek manuscripts also omit "Jesus" as an explicit subject here, as well as in 4:18 and 4:23.
notes.4:13: The Greek text spells the town Nazara, an early Greek form of Nazareth.
notes.4:24: The Greek participle seleniazomenous ("epileptics") literally means "moon-struck," an ancient term for epilepsy and convulsive seizures.
notes.5:18: Greek 'iota' denotes the smallest letter of the alphabet (corresponding to Hebrew yod), and 'stroke of a letter' (keraia) denotes a tiny pen stroke or projection distinguishing similar Hebrew letters.
notes.5:22: The critical Greek text omits 'without a cause' (eike), found in some later manuscripts. 'Raca' is an Aramaic term of contempt meaning 'empty-headed,' and 'hell' renders Greek Gehenna, the Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem.
notes.5:37: The Greek phrase 'from the evil one' (ek tou ponerou) may also be understood as neuter, 'from evil,' since both genders share the same genitive form.
notes.5:44: The critical Greek text preserves the shorter form of this command, without the expanded clauses ('bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you...') found in later manuscripts and paralleled in Luke 6:27-28.
notes.6:11: The Greek adjective epiousios is exceedingly rare in ancient Greek and appears in the New Testament only here and in Luke 11:3; it is traditionally rendered "daily," though it may also mean "for the coming day" or "necessary for subsistence."
notes.6:13: The Greek phrase tou ponerou may be understood as either "the evil one" (masculine) or "evil" (neuter). Following the earliest Greek manuscripts, the later liturgical doxology ("For Yours is the kingdom...") is absent from the critical text.
notes.6:22: In Jewish idiom, a "sound" (Greek haplous, also "single" or "clear") eye signifies generosity and undivided devotion, whereas an "evil" (Greek poneros) eye in verse 23 denotes envy or stinginess.
notes.6:27: The Greek noun helikia can refer either to physical "stature" or to "span of life"; retaining the literal measure "one cubit" (roughly eighteen inches) preserves the Greek wording.
notes.7:6: "What is holy" recalls consecrated food from the altar and figuratively denotes sacred truths, warning disciples not to expose precious spiritual realities to hostile scorn.
notes.7:14: The critical Greek text reads hoti ("for" or "because"), continuing the explanation from verse 13, whereas some manuscripts read the exclamatory ti ("How narrow is the gate!").
notes.7:29: Following the critical Greek text, "their scribes" (rather than "the scribes") sharpens the contrast between Jesus' own authority and the derivative instruction of the people's religious teachers.
notes.8:10: The critical Greek text reads "with no one in Israel have I found such great faith," whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read "not even in Israel have I found so great a faith."
notes.8:15: The critical Greek text reads "to Him" (singular), depicting Peter's mother-in-law ministering directly to Jesus, while later manuscripts read "to them."
notes.8:24: The Greek noun seismos ("tempest") literally denotes a violent shaking or earthquake, underscoring the sudden, turbulent upheaval upon the sea.
notes.8:28: The earliest Greek manuscripts of Matthew read "Gadarenes," referring to the territory of Gadara southeast of the Sea of Galilee; later manuscripts substitute "Gergesenes" or "Gerasenes" (cf. Mark 5:1; Luke 8:26).
notes.9:4: The critical text reads idon ("seeing"), highlighting Jesus' direct perception of the scribes' inward thoughts, whereas later manuscripts read eidos ("knowing").
notes.9:8: The earliest manuscripts read "were struck with fear" (ephobethesan), expressing reverent awe before divine authority; later Byzantine manuscripts read "marveled."
notes.9:13: The critical Greek text ends with "sinners"; the additional phrase "to repentance" in later manuscripts reflects harmonization with Luke 5:32.
notes.9:36: The Greek participles eskylmenoi ("harassed," literally "flayed" or "troubled") and errimmenoi ("cast down" or "helpless") depict the crowds as spiritually exhausted and neglected like untended sheep.
notes.10:4: "Cananaean" transliterates Greek Kananaios (from Aramaic qan'an, meaning "Zealot"), identifying Simon's zealot affiliation rather than Canaanite ancestry.
notes.10:25: "Beelzebul" follows the Greek critical text (ending in -l rather than -b), a name applied in Jewish usage to the prince of demons.
notes.10:28: "hell" translates Greek geenna (Gehenna), referring to the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem as the emblem of final judgment.
notes.10:29: "a small copper coin" translates Greek assarion, a Roman bronze coin valued at one-sixteenth of a denarius.
notes.11:2: "through his disciples" follows the Greek critical text (dia); later manuscripts read "two of his disciples" (dyo).
notes.11:12: "suffers violence" translates Greek biazetai as a passive; some understand it as a middle verb ("presses forward forcefully"), with the following clause referring either to hostile opponents or to earnest seekers.
notes.11:19: "by her works" follows the Greek critical text (ergon), echoing "the works of the Christ" in 11:2; later manuscripts read "by her children" (teknon), aligning with Luke 7:35.
notes.11:23: "will you be exalted to heaven? You shall descend to Hades!" follows the critical text's rhetorical question expecting a negative answer (me ... hypsothese; ... katabese), rather than the later reading "who are exalted to heaven, shall be brought down to Hades."
notes.12:4: The Greek critical text reads the plural "they ate" (referring to David and his companions), whereas later manuscripts assimilate to the singular "he ate." "The showbread" renders the Greek expression "the loaves of presentation" set before God in the sanctuary (Leviticus 24:5-9).
notes.12:6: "Something greater" translates a neuter Greek adjective, pointing to the messianic kingdom and divine presence embodied in Jesus Himself (compare the parallel neuter expressions in verses 41 and 42).
notes.12:24: "Beelzebul" follows the Greek text as the title of the ruler of the demons, rather than the Latin-influenced spelling "Beelzebub."
notes.12:40: "The great fish" renders the Greek word ketos (also used in the Septuagint of Jonah 2:1), which denotes a massive sea creature or sea monster.
notes.12:47: A few early Greek manuscripts omit this verse, likely due to a scribal eye-skip from "to speak" at the end of verse 46 to the same verb at the end of verse 47, though it is strongly attested across the manuscript tradition.
notes.13:25: Greek zizania ("tares") refers specifically to darnel (Lolium temulentum), a noxious weed whose early blades closely resemble wheat until the grain heads appear.
notes.13:33: Greek sata tria ("three measures") denotes three seahs of flour, roughly half a bushel (about thirty-six to forty liters), sufficient to bake bread for a large gathering.
notes.13:35: Matthew cites Psalm 78:2 (LXX 77:2), attributed to Asaph, whom 2 Chronicles 29:30 calls a seer; the critical text retains "of the world" at the close of the verse.
notes.13:51: Following the critical text, this verse omits "Jesus said to them" at the opening and "Lord" after "Yes," continuing Jesus's direct speech without interruption from verse 50.
notes.14:9: This Greek text omits a contrastive conjunction between the king's grief and his oaths, requiring a strong punctuation break and 'yet' in English to convey the contrast.
notes.14:12: The Greek shifts from the neuter noun for 'corpse' to the masculine pronoun 'him,' underscoring the personal dignity of John's burial.
notes.14:24: This Greek text reads 'already in the midst of the sea,' whereas some manuscripts read 'many stadia distant from the land.'
notes.14:27: The Greek phrase rendered 'it is I' serves both as ordinary self-identification and as an echo of the Old Testament divine self-revelation 'I am.'
notes.14:29: This Greek text reads 'and came toward Jesus,' indicating that Peter actually walked toward Him before sinking, rather than the variant reading 'to go to Jesus.'
notes.15:5: Greek doron ("gift") refers to a vow dedicating property or support to God (called Corban in Mark 7:11), which Pharisaic tradition treated as releasing a person from the obligation to provide for parents.
notes.15:14: Following the Greek critical text, Jesus calls the Pharisees "blind guides" without the addition "of the blind" found in later manuscripts.
notes.15:39: The Greek critical text reads "Magadan," a locality on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, where later manuscripts read "Magdala."
notes.16:3: The weather-discernment saying in verses 2b-3 is absent from the earliest manuscripts (such as Sinaiticus and Vaticanus); the critical text omits verse 2b and places verse 3 in double brackets to mark its uncertain textual standing.
notes.16:18: Jesus plays on the Greek words Petros ("Peter," a stone) and petra ("rock," bedrock); "Hades" translates Greek Hades, the realm of the dead.
notes.16:19: The Greek future periphrastic perfect constructions ("shall be bound" and "shall be loosed") may also be rendered "shall have been bound" and "shall have been loosed."
notes.16:21: The Greek critical text reads "Jesus Christ" here (supported by early witnesses including Sinaiticus and Vaticanus), whereas many later manuscripts read simply "Jesus."
notes.16:25: The same Greek word psyche is rendered "life" in verse 25 and "soul" in verse 26, encompassing both physical life and one's eternal self.
notes.17:15: Greek seleniazetai (literally "is moonstruck") was the standard ancient term for epilepsy or convulsive seizures.
notes.17:20: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "little faith" (oligopistian) rather than "unbelief" and omit verse 21, which later scribes appear to have assimilated from Mark 9:29.
notes.17:22: The critical Greek text reads systrephomenon ("gathering together"), whereas later manuscripts read anastrephomenon ("staying" or "traveling about").
notes.17:24: The two-drachma tax (didrachma) was the annual half-shekel temple tax (Exod 30:13); the "stater" in verse 27 was a four-drachma silver coin, exact payment for two men.
notes.18:6: Greek mylos onikos literally denotes a heavy millstone turned by a donkey, far larger than a household hand mill.
notes.18:10: The earliest and best Greek manuscripts omit verse 11 ("For the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost"), which appears to be a later harmonization from Luke 19:10.
notes.18:15: The earliest Greek witnesses omit "against you" (eis se), broadening the counsel to address any sin committed by a fellow believer.
notes.18:22: Greek hebdomēkontakis hepta can mean either "seventy-seven times" (echoing the Septuagint of Gen 4:24 and reversing Lamech's vengeance) or "seventy times seven."
notes.19:9: The final clause ("and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery") is present in the Greek text translated here (supported by Codex Vaticanus, Codex Ephraemi, and the Majority Text), though omitted in some witnesses such as Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Bezae.
notes.19:17: The Greek text reads "Why do you ask Me concerning what is good? There is One who is good" (alongside "Teacher" rather than "Good Teacher" in 19:16), reflecting the earliest Matthean manuscripts; later manuscripts harmonize the wording with Mark 10:17-18 and Luke 18:18-19.
notes.19:28: "Regeneration" translates the Greek palingenesia, signifying the eschatological renewal and restoration of all creation at the coming of the Son of Man in glory.
notes.19:29: The Greek text translated here retains both "or wife" and "a hundredfold," whereas some early manuscripts omit "or wife" or read "manifold" (pollaplasiona).
notes.20:2: A denarius was a standard Roman silver coin equivalent to a day's wage for a common laborer.
notes.20:15: "Is your eye evil" renders a Semitic idiom expressing envy, jealousy, or a begrudging spirit toward another's generosity.
notes.20:16: The earliest Greek manuscripts end the verse here; later manuscripts add "for many are called, but few are chosen," harmonizing with Matthew 22:14.
notes.20:22: The earliest manuscripts do not include the reference to being baptized with Jesus's baptism in verses 22-23, which later witnesses imported from Mark 10:38-39.
notes.21:5: Matthew combines Isaiah 62:11 with Zechariah 9:9, rendering the poetic parallelism of Zechariah literally with both a donkey and a colt, matching the two animals brought in verses 2 and 7.
notes.21:16: Jesus quotes Psalm 8:2 following the Greek Septuagint reading ("You have prepared praise") rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("You have ordained strength").
notes.21:31: Ancient manuscripts differ in the order of the two sons in verses 28–31; the Saints Greek Critical Text places the initially refusing yet obedient son first, leading to the answer "The first."
notes.21:41: The Greek uses an emphatic wordplay, kakous kakos apolesei (literally, "wicked men wickedly he will destroy"), captured here as "bring those wretches to a wretched end."
notes.21:44: Although omitted by a small number of Western manuscripts (such as Codex Bezae), this verse is strongly attested across the major textual traditions and is retained in the Saints Greek Critical Text.
notes.22:9: The Greek phrase tas diexodous ton hodon literally denotes the outlets where city roads open out onto the main highways, rendered here as "the main thoroughfares."
notes.22:13: The Greek text reads "Bind his feet and hands and cast him out," without the later Byzantine expansion "take him away and," and uses diakonoi ("attendants") rather than douloi ("servants") as in verses 3–10.
notes.22:30: The Greek text reads "as angels in heaven," without the later addition "of God" found in some manuscripts.
notes.22:44: The Greek text reads hypokato ton podon sou ("beneath Your feet") rather than hypopodion ton podon sou ("the footstool of Your feet"), which appears in later manuscripts harmonized to Psalm 110:1 (LXX 109:1).
notes.23:8: The Greek text here reads kathegetes ("Instructor" or "Teacher"), matching verse 10, rather than didaskalos ("Teacher") with the later addition "the Christ."
notes.23:13: Verse 14 ("Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you devour widows' houses...") is absent from the earliest manuscripts and from this Greek text, having entered later copies from Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47.
notes.23:15: "Hell" translates Greek Gehenna (from the Hebrew Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem), used in the Gospels for the place of final divine judgment; the same word appears in verse 33.
notes.23:35: Zechariah the priest, son of Jehoiada, was stoned in the temple court in 2 Chronicles 24:20-22 (the final book of the Hebrew canon), whereas the prophet Zechariah was son of Berechiah (Zechariah 1:1); the statement spans the martyrs from the first to the last book of the Hebrew Scriptures.
notes.24:7: The critical Greek text reads "famines and earthquakes," without the addition "and pestilences" found in later Byzantine manuscripts (cf. Luke 21:11).
notes.24:28: The Greek word aetoi can denote either eagles or carrion-eating vultures (such as the griffon vulture); "vultures" fits the proverb's mention of a carcass.
notes.24:33: The Greek verb estin ("is") has no expressed subject and may refer either to the Son of Man ("He is near") or to His coming and the end ("it is near").
notes.24:36: The phrase "nor the Son" (oude ho huios) is strongly attested in the earliest manuscripts and preserved in the critical text, though omitted in many later manuscripts.
notes.24:42: The critical Greek text reads "what day" (poia hemera) rather than "what hour" (poia hora), which appears in later manuscripts by assimilation to verse 44.
notes.25:6: The Greek text omits "is coming" (found in later manuscripts) and ends literally "go out to a meeting," rendered idiomatically as "Go forth to meet him!"
notes.25:13: The Greek text ends with "nor the hour," without the later expansion "in which the Son of Man is coming."
notes.25:15: In the Greek text, the adverb "immediately" stands after the sentence stop at the end of verse 15 and syntactically opens the action of the first servant in verse 16.
notes.25:31: The Greek text reads "all the angels" without the adjective "holy" present in later manuscripts.
notes.26:15: The Greek verb estesan literally means "weighed out," echoing the Septuagint wording of Zechariah 11:12 and reflecting the ancient custom of weighing silver bullion or coinage.
notes.26:25: Jesus's reply "You have said so" (Greek Sy eipas) is a formal Semitic idiom of guarded affirmation that confirms the truth of Judas's question while placing its weight back upon him.
notes.26:28: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads "My blood of the covenant" without "new," following the earliest manuscripts and directly echoing Exodus 24:8.
notes.26:31: Jesus cites Zechariah 13:7 with the verb rendered in the first-person singular ("I will strike"), attributing the striking of the Shepherd to God's sovereign purpose.
notes.26:45: The Greek verbs katheudete and anapauesthe have the same form in both the indicative and imperative moods, allowing either a question ("Are you still sleeping and taking your rest?") or an ironic command ("Sleep on now and take your rest").
notes.26:50: Jesus's elliptical words (Greek eph' ho parei, literally "for which you are here") are punctuated as a statement in the Saints Greek Critical Text, implying "do that for which you have come," though some read the clause as a question ("Why have you come?").
notes.26:64: "The Power" (Greek tes dynameos) is a reverent Jewish circumlocution for God; Jesus weaves together Psalm 110:1 and Daniel 7:13 to declare His messianic vindication.
notes.27:6: The Greek word korbonan is an Aramaic loanword denoting the sacred temple treasury where consecrated offerings were kept.
notes.27:9: Matthew attributes this composite citation to Jeremiah, weaving language from Zechariah 11:12–13 together with potter and field imagery from Jeremiah (such as Jeremiah 18–19 and 32:6–15).
notes.27:24: The critical Greek text reads simply "of this blood," without the clarifying phrase "of this righteous Man" found in later manuscripts.
notes.27:32: The Greek verb translated "pressed into service" (angareuo) is a technical term for Roman military requisitioning of civilians to bear loads (compare Matthew 5:41).
notes.27:35: The critical Greek text ends after "by casting lots," omitting the explicit quotation of Psalm 22:18 found in later manuscripts (compare John 19:24).
notes.27:46: The critical Greek text reads the Aramaic form "Eloi" (matching Mark 15:34) rather than the Hebrew "Eli" found in other manuscripts, quoting Psalm 22:1.
notes.27:54: In Greek, the phrase "Son of God" (theou huios) lacks the definite article; while Matthew's Gospel points to the definite confession "the Son of God," the centurion's words can also be read qualitatively as "a son of God."
notes.27:65: The Greek verb echete can be read either as an indicative ("You have a guard") or as an imperative ("Take a guard").
notes.28:1: The Greek phrase opse de sabbaton can mean "late on the Sabbath," but in Hellenistic Greek opse with the genitive commonly means "after," which aligns here with the dawning of the first day of the week.
notes.28:6: The Greek critical text reads simply "where He lay," omitting the clarifying title "the Lord" found in later manuscripts.
notes.28:9: Greek chairete serves both as a standard greeting ("Greetings!") and literally as a call to "Rejoice!"; the critical text also omits the later scribal expansion "And as they went to tell His disciples" at the opening of the verse.
notes.28:17: The Greek construction hoi de edistasan ("yet some doubted" or "hesitated") lacks an explicit contrasting "some" in the first clause, so interpreters debate whether only a portion of the eleven hesitated or whether all experienced a mixture of worship and uncertainty.
notes.28:20: The phrase "all the days" literally renders pasas tas hemeras (often smoothed to "always"), "the close of the age" renders synteleias tou aionos, and the critical text concludes without the later liturgical addition "Amen."
